    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Top Wall Street analysts are bullish on the growth potential of these 3 stocks

    📅 18 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (942 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Fears around the artificial intelligence trade and higher pressure on oil prices are weighing on global markets, but a few stocks offer investors solid growth prospects even in choppy times.
    • Investors with a long-term horizon can look beyond the ongoing volatility and track the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts to pick attractive stocks with strong long-term growth potential.
    • Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Fears around the artificial intelligence trade and higher pressure on oil prices are weighing on global markets, but a few stocks offer investors solid growth prospects even in choppy times.

    Investors with a long-term horizon can look beyond the ongoing volatility and track the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts to pick attractive stocks with strong long-term growth potential.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Health insurer UnitedHealth delivered better-than-expected results for the third quarter of 2026. The company also raised its full-year earnings outlook, reflecting continued progress on its turnaround strategy.

    According to recent reports, following the Q3 print, Morgan Stanley analyst Erin Wright reiterated a buy rating on UNH stock with a price target of $529. "UNH's beat & raise reinforces turnaround momentum, with improving MA [Medicare Advantage]/Optum Health supporting a higher '26 EPS baseline & upside to '27 consensus," said Wright.

    According to recent reports, the five-star analyst added that better-than-expected performance in the UnitedHealthcare and Optum Health businesses supported another upgrade to the company's 2026 adjusted earnings per share outlook to at least $20.50. Wright noted that UNH raised the earnings guidance despite incremental investments planned for the fourth quarter of 2026.

    In a recent development, furthermore, Wright highlighted management's view that the consensus 2027 EPS of $22.63 was too conservative. Reaching even the low end of the company's 13% to 16% long-term EPS growth target would imply an EPS of $23.17.

    Wright raised her 2026 EPS estimate to $20.65 from $19.82 and 2027 EPS to $23.24 from $22.54, reflecting the latest upside and an improving 2026 medical loss ratio to 87.4% from 88.1%. Overall, she believes that UNH's operational performance continues to improve, increasing her confidence in its UHC strategy and Optum Health turnaround execution.

    It has been revealed that wright ranks No. 264 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. Her ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 15%. See UnitedHealth Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Industry observers note that social media giant Meta Platforms has been making headlines since the launch of its Muse AI agent, which is seeing solid traction. Investors look forward to updates on the tech giant's AI strategy when it announces its third-quarter results on Oct. 21.

    Heading into Q3 earnings, Guggenheim analyst Michael Morris maintained a buy rating on Meta stock and increased his price target to $850 from $700, reflecting higher estimates for 2027. He expects Muse usage momentum and engagement levels to shape investor sentiment into the Q3 earnings call.

    Sources indicate that specifically, Morris highlighted that, according to Apptopia, Muse reached 1.3 million daily active users in five weeks versus 300,000 in the first week. Given that Muse's current adoption represents less than 0.05% of Meta's 3.6 billion daily active user base, the analyst expects management to prioritize boosting usage over near-term monetization.

    Sources indicate that "Over time, we believe Muse monetizes primarily through businesses paying to reach consumers through their agents, consistent with the economics of Meta's core advertising business, rather than consumer wallets," said the five-star analyst. He added that the checkout integrations with Shopify and PayPal reflect this framework.

    While there are concerns that a rival could overtake Muse or the recently debuted Muse Wonder and push Meta into a prolonged cycle of overinvestment, Morris remains bullish due to the manufacturer's strong record in scaling WhatsApp and competing strongly with TikTok via Reels as well as free distribution to an extensive user base.

    Sources indicate that morris ranks No. 629 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 13.2%. See Meta Platforms KPIs on TipRanks.

    Next is semiconductor manufacturer Marvell Technology. Earlier this month, Marvell held its Investor Day, where it raised its total addressable market estimate to $400 billion by 2030, reflecting solid AI-led demand tailwinds.

    After hosting a non-deal roadshow with Marvell's senior management following the Investor Day, Stifel analyst Tore Svanberg reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $370.

    The five-star analyst noted that a major focus of the roadshow was the XPU and XPU Attach mix, as Marvell's Custom business expands toward its FY31 revenue target of $30 billion. In this regard, management reiterated that it expects a balanced mix of XPU and XPU Attach revenue in FY31, though it noted that either segment could grow rapidly enough to shift the mix toward 60/40 or 40/60.

    While XPU drove most of the nearly $1.5 billion Custom revenue in FY26, Svanberg expects Marvell's XPU Attach business to grow substantially through the end of the decade, leading to a more balanced mix in this business. At the Investor Day event, the organization raised its FY29 Custom target from more than $10 billion to over $12 billion, mainly driven by strength in the XPU Attach business.

    Recent findings suggest that svanberg stated that another key topic in the roadshow was whether Marvell can secure enough capacity to meet its raised targets. Management said that it met with suppliers ahead of Investor Day to share its five-year goals and received commitments to support these targets. The analyst believes that Marvell's supply chain commitments give it a competitive edge over rivals as customers seek reliable partners for large-scale infrastructure buildouts.

    Recent findings suggest that svanberg ranks No. 91 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 58% of the time, delivering an average return of 31.8%. See Marvell Technology Statistics on TipRanks.

    #130823. Retirees face a looming deadline for required withdrawals — missing it could trigger a tax penalty

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (635 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Retirees face a looming deadline for required withdrawals — missing it could trigger a tax penalty

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (635 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that every year, millions of Americans must take required withdrawals from retirement accounts by Dec.
    • Amid the busy holiday season, it's easy to miss the year-end deadline for required minimum distributions — a mistake that can trigger a hefty IRS penalty, experts stated.
    • "One of the most common RMD mistakes is waiting until the last minute," remarked certified financial planner Alex Canellopoulos, director of wealth at Vista Capital Partners in Portland, Oregon.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that every year, millions of Americans must take required withdrawals from retirement accounts by Dec. 31.

    Amid the busy holiday season, it's easy to miss the year-end deadline for required minimum distributions — a mistake that can trigger a hefty IRS penalty, experts stated.

    "One of the most common RMD mistakes is waiting until the last minute," remarked certified financial planner Alex Canellopoulos, director of wealth at Vista Capital Partners in Portland, Oregon.

    Most retirees must start RMDs from pretax accounts at age 73. The withdrawal is based on the previous year's account balances on Dec. 31, your age and an IRS "life expectancy factor.".

    The first annual RMD deadline is April 1 of the year after you turn 73, and future withdrawals are due by Dec. 31. If you wait until April 1 for the first one, you'll need two RMDs that year.

    RMDs also apply to certain inherited IRAs if the original IRA owner reached RMD age before their death.

    In 2023, more than 14.8 million taxpayers age 70 or older had a traditional individual retirement account, according to the latest IRS data. The average year-end market value of the accounts was about $330,000.

    Deferring RMDs until the last minute raises the likelihood of mistakes, such as overlooking certain retirement accounts or making withdrawal calculation errors, Canellopoulos noted.

    Some 7% of Vanguard investors at RMD age missed their yearly withdrawal in 2025, up slightly from 6.7% in 2024, according to a Vanguard analysis of about 400,000 RMD-age retirees with IRA balances published in December 2025.

    Among those investors, the average missed RMD was $10,500 in 2025, Vanguard told CNBC.

    Industry observers note that investors who don't take RMDs by the annual deadline may owe an excise tax to the IRS, worth up to 25% of the amount they should have withdrawn. For example, the excise tax could be up to $2,625 for a $10,500 missed RMD.

    If investors miss a required withdrawal, they could reduce the penalty to 10% if they "timely corrected" the RMD within two years and file Form 5329, according to the IRS.

    In some cases, the IRS could waive the penalty entirely due to "reasonable error" if investors take "reasonable steps" to fix the shortfall, according to the agency. Investors can file Form 5329 with a letter of explanation to request the waiver.

    "If you don't ask, you're not going to get it," said certified public accountant Tim Steffen, director of advanced planning at financial services firm Baird. "I've never heard of anybody being denied the waiver.".

    Investors who give to charity may be skipping a specific donation strategy that can reduce or eliminate their annual RMDs, according to Lawrence Pon, a CFP and CPA based in Redwood City, California.

    They can use a so-called qualified charitable distribution, or QCD, Pon said.

    A QCD has a dual tax benefit: It doesn't count as taxable income and may also satisfy at least part of an investor's yearly RMD, Pon stated.

    The move requires a direct transfer from an investor's pretax IRA to an eligible nonprofit organization. They can donate up to $111,000 in 2026. While QCD eligibility begins at age 70½, transfers won't start counting toward RMDs until an investor reaches their RMD age.

    It has been revealed that generally, taxpayers only get a tax break for large charitable donations if they itemize deductions on their tax returns. But QCDs still provide a tax benefit for charitable gifts when investors use the standard deduction.

    QCDs "provide a real benefit if you are not itemizing [tax deductions]," said Pon.

    While there's no tax deduction for QCDs, the transfer won't increase a taxpayer's adjusted gross income, or AGI. Raising AGI can cause other tax consequences, such as higher premiums for Medicare Part B and Part D.

    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Nvidia stock plunges 14%, wraps up longest weekly losing streak since 2008 financial crisis

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (485 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The last time Wall Street was this down on Nvidia the chipmaker's flagship product was the GeForce graphics processor for high-end PC video games, and markets were reeling from the global financial crisis.
    • It has been revealed that nvidia shares tumbled 14% on Friday, sliding for a seventh straight day as investors grew increasingly concerned about life after co-founder Jensen Huang.
    • Shares of Nvidia are down 46% over the period, pushing the company's market cap down by about $2.6 trillion.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The last time Wall Street was this down on Nvidia the chipmaker's flagship product was the GeForce graphics processor for high-end PC video games, and markets were reeling from the global financial crisis.

    It has been revealed that nvidia shares tumbled 14% on Friday, sliding for a seventh straight day as investors grew increasingly concerned about life after co-founder Jensen Huang. The stock closed lower for a seventh consecutive week, the longest such stretch since 2008.

    Shares of Nvidia are down 46% over the period, pushing the company's market cap down by about $2.6 trillion. The stock is now trading at roughly 8.4 times forward earnings, while Advanced Micro Devices is valued at 29 times profit for the next 12 months.

    On Friday, Reuters reported that the Securities and Exchange Commission is exploring potential accounting issues at Nvidia, pushing the stock down further.

    Once the most valuable company in the world, Nvidia now has a market cap of $3 trillion, putting it fourth behind Apple, Microsoft and Alphabet.

    It has been revealed that nvidia is reeling from the removal of Huang, who resigned on Nov. 12, after multiple reported affairs, including one with a Chinese businesswoman who was allegedly a spy.

    Harvey Jones, Nvidia's newly appointed board chair, said earlier this week that Huang had resigned after "disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the manufacturer's code of conduct, standards and cultural norms.".

    But the chipmaker's losing streak started before Nvidia was thrown into crisis as investors worried over the sustainability of the AI buildout, particularly after the midterm elections, and emerging competition in AI chips from Google and AMD.

    Even a better-than-expected earnings report, which included an increase to fiscal 2028 guidance, didn't stem the selling. Interim CEO Colette Kress, the manufacturer's longtime CFO, projected revenue growth next fiscal year of 75%, and mentioned that customers aren't going anywhere.

    On Tuesday's earnings call with analysts, Kress signed off by saying, "we've got this." In a company meeting the next day, executives told staff that it was moving its yearly review process, which can come with more stock, from March to December.

    Sources indicate that for investors, one major question is whether Nvidia can continue to innovate and sustain its commanding lead in the AI chip market without its visionary leader. Almost the entire firm now is built around the AI trade, a phenomenon that began taking hold just four years ago with the launch of OpenAI's ChatGPT.

    Before that, Nvidia's primary business was selling graphics cards used for video games. In mid-2008, the last time the stock was this deep into a weekly losing streak, Nvidia was generating less than $1 billion per quarter. Now it pulls in more than $1 billion per day. At the time, the entire market was in freefall due to the worst financial crisis since the Great Depression.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that global stock markets remain volatile amid persistent geopolitical tensions and concerns about the sustainability of AI trade.
    • Tracking recommendations from top Wall Street analysts can help investors pick attractive stocks, as these experts assess a company's ability to pay dividends consistently.
    • Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that global stock markets remain volatile amid persistent geopolitical tensions and concerns about the sustainability of AI trade. Given this backdrop, investors seeking steady income can add dividend-paying stocks to their portfolios.

    Tracking recommendations from top Wall Street analysts can help investors pick attractive stocks, as these experts assess a company's ability to pay dividends consistently.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    In a recent development, integrated oil and gas giant Chevron (CVX) is a dividend king. The organization has increased its dividend for 39 consecutive years. At a quarterly dividend of $1.78 per share (annualized dividend of $7.12 per share), CVX offers a yield of 3.14%. Chevron will announce its third-quarter results on October 30.

    It has been revealed that in an earnings preview note on U.S. oil majors, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on Chevron with a price target of $241. The analyst is focused on the manufacturer's international growth prospects across Latin America, the Middle East, West Africa, and the Eastern Mediterranean.

    Sources indicate that specifically, Mehta highlighted management's commentary on solid execution in Venezuela, with gross production expected to more than double to nearly 600 kbd (kilo barrels per day) by 2031 via three joint ventures. He also noted a recent oil and gas condensate discovery in offshore Angola and is awaiting commercial updates on the West Qurna 2 and Nasiriyah projects in Iraq.

    Furthermore, Mehta expects CVX to report improved productivity and capital efficiency across domestic shale assets. He expects the improvement mainly in the Permian Basin, where Chevron projects advanced chemical treatments to drive about a 10% recovery uplift in latest wells and bring down capital spend per barrel by about 25% year-over-year. Overall, Mehta expects Chevron to report Q3 2026 EPS of $4.95, above the consensus of $4.89.

    It has been revealed that "While unfavorable timing effects and volatile commodity prices may present quarterly earnings headwinds, we highlight healthy U.S. refining margins and strong asset utilization as partial offsets," stated Mehta.

    Sources indicate that mehta ranks No. 381 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Chevron KPIs on TipRanks.

    Recent findings suggest that kinetik Holdings (KNTK) is a fully integrated, pure-play, midstream tech giant operating in the Delaware Basin. Earlier this month, the company declared a dividend of $0.81 per share, payable on October 30, 2026. With an annualized dividend of $3.24 per share, KNTK offers a yield of 5.82%. Kinetik will announce its Q3 earnings on November 4, with a conference call scheduled the next day.

    Ahead of Q3 2026 earnings, Goldman Sachs analyst John Mackay reiterated a buy rating on Kinetik stock and slightly raised his price target to $58 from $57. He expects the company to report Q3 2026 EBITDA of $279 million, higher than the Street's expectation of $270 million but lower than the second quarter's EBITDA of $281 million.

    Recent findings suggest that the 5-star analyst expects Kinetik's Q3 performance to gain from higher gas volumes after notable curtailments in the second quarter. Mackay also expects the quarter to benefit from higher production and steady commodity margins, even though some lower-margin contracts and weaker Waha spread marketing gains could weigh on results.

    Overall, Mackay increased his Q3 2026 estimates to reflect higher volumes, driven by rapid Permian egress pipeline commissioning, stronger throughput at Kings Landing I, and higher M2M commodity prices, offset by increased costs.

    "As natural gas takeaway constraints ease across the Permian, investor focus centers on KNTK's YE26 volume trajectory and durability of its multi-year growth," mentioned Mackay.

    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    How China is using summits to expand its global influence

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • SHENZHEN, China — For a second year in a row, Chinese President Xi Jinping has brought Russian President Vladimir Putin together with another major world leader on mainland Chinese shores.
    • President Donald Trump had a trilateral meeting with Xi and Putin on Thursday, after the three met the prior evening during a welcome banquet for the Asia-Pacific Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen.
    • In September 2025, Xi, Putin and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi briefly laughed together for a friendly photo-op alongside an annual meeting of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization in Tianjin, China.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    SHENZHEN, China — For a second year in a row, Chinese President Xi Jinping has brought Russian President Vladimir Putin together with another major world leader on mainland Chinese shores.

    U.S. President Donald Trump had a trilateral meeting with Xi and Putin on Thursday, after the three met the prior evening during a welcome banquet for the Asia-Pacific Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen. It marked the first time they had met together in person.

    In September 2025, Xi, Putin and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi briefly laughed together for a friendly photo-op alongside an annual meeting of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization in Tianjin, China. The gathering followed easing tensions between Beijing and Newly introduced Delhi.

    Sources indicate that china's "ability to engage directly with the world major powers" reflects the country's influence across the Global South and Eurasia, said Jodie Wen, postdoctoral fellow at the Center for International Security and Strategy at Tsinghua University. "China hopes to play a more constructive role in this conflict-[ridden], unstable world.".

    In the future, "China will hope to provide more platforms" within its borders for countries to discuss challenges, she remarked.

    Trump, Xi, Putin said they blueprint to boost oil production, revamp UN after trilateral talks.

    Recent findings suggest that I watched Trump, Xi and Putin gather in China. Here are my top takeaways.

    Trump holds talks separately with Putin and Xi ahead of their historic trilateral meeting.

    Takaichi gets chilly reception in China on first Japan leader visit since 2019.

    Why the Middle East is watching the Trump-Xi-Putin summit.

    Trump arrives in China for historic meeting with Xi, Putin.

    China's Xi calls for removing trade and investment barriers.

    Putin claims EU is losing industry, falling behind competition.

    Three things to watch as Trump, Xi and Putin meet in China.

    China has increasingly played the role of broker, for instance, providing the forum for restoring diplomatic ties between Saudi Arabia and Iran in 2023.

    According to recent reports, by participating in and hosting different multilateral organizations, China has stayed in the Western orbit while cultivating relations with non-Western countries. The two photo-ops last year and this year reflect only a portion of Xi's large number of meetings with different world leaders.

    Industry observers note that xi has hosted more than 40 heads of state so far this year, including at least eight around the APEC meetings in Shenzhen this week. That's on top of receiving over 60 state visits in 2025, according to CNBC analysis of official Chinese readouts.

    Domestic Chinese media have highlighted how Xi has met with many foreign leaders around the China-hosted events.

    "Beijing sees these multilateral platforms as opportunities to expand its international influence and demonstrate its commitment to multilateralism, while bilateral diplomacy remains equally notable," said Yue Su, principal economist for China at EIU.

    But she noted that different countries increasingly pursue different geopolitical and economic priorities, making it challenging to reach consensus even through multilateral organizations.

    "Against this backdrop, China's diplomatic priorities are increasingly focused on delivering tangible economic benefits through trade, investment, financial connectivity and technology cooperation," she remarked.

    In a recent development, on Thursday, Xi announced at the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting that China would provide $20 million in support for the Asia Pacific region. He also advocated for the development of an "Asia-Pacific community with a shared future," an iteration of his commonly used slogan on a "shared future" for humanity more broadly.

    According to recent reports, the Shenzhen summit can create meaningful outcomes for crisis management, as well as diplomatic space for future negotiations, Tsinghua University's Wen said. She added that it's important for leaders to come together in person in order to avoid misunderstandings and further tensions.

    In a recent development, trump mentioned Thursday at the trilateral that the U.S., China and Russia are "uniquely positioned" to discuss reducing nuclear weapons at their historic meeting. A Chinese readout subsequently said the three leaders discussed Ukraine, the Middle East and the Korean Peninsula.

    —CNBC's Matthew Tan contributed to this report.

    #130804. I never wanted the American Dream and I felt like something was wrong with me—until I moved abroad

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1016 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    I never wanted the American Dream and I felt like something was wrong with me—until I moved abroad

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1016 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • I got my first job at 17, working the register at an Eckerd's drugstore in Texas.
    • It all felt suffocating: the added responsibility, the longer hours, the idea that this was the ladder I was supposed to want to climb.
    • Sources indicate that I never wanted the American Dream I saw so many people around me striving to achieve.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    I got my first job at 17, working the register at an Eckerd's drugstore in Texas. My manager was only a few years older than me, and while my coworkers seemed motivated by the idea of working their way up to his position, I felt no desire to follow that path.

    It all felt suffocating: the added responsibility, the longer hours, the idea that this was the ladder I was supposed to want to climb. I wanted to work, but I couldn't wrap my head around building my whole identity around a job.

    Sources indicate that I never wanted the American Dream I saw so many people around me striving to achieve. For a long time, I wondered if something was wrong with me. It wasn't until I finally made a long-term move abroad about a decade ago that I realized it was okay to want something different.

    In a recent development, after college, I got a job in travel sales. I was good at it. Talking about travel all day suited the wanderlust I'd carried since my first trip abroad in my teens.

    I continued working in sales, marketing and the odd temp role for years. But they were always just jobs. I didn't feel like they defined me or feel a calling to an industry or title the way people around me seemed to.

    Sources indicate that of course, I wanted financial stability, but I was unwilling to sacrifice my time and well-being to get it. I just didn't connect with the version of ambition that meant grinding toward a corner office. What I wanted the most wasn't status; it was freedom, growth and upcoming experiences.

    It has been revealed that the wanderlust eventually caught up to me, and at 26 I moved to Spain to teach English. Even though I was working, people saw it as taking a year off from my career and warned me it could damage my resume. I simply didn't care. Living for my resume had never made sense to me.

    It has been revealed that looking back, I think being abroad offered an escape from the pressure to chase the traditional path of the American Dream. There, I felt free to enjoy life and figure out who I was without worrying about what box I needed to tick next.

    Recent findings suggest that I wanted to stay in Spain, but I couldn't find a visa that would let me live there long-term, so I returned to the U.S. I became a serial job hopper for almost 10 years, quitting a job every year to spend summers visiting friends in the Netherlands, the U.K. and Switzerland or solo traveling in Spain on the money I'd saved up.

    On the personal side, I wasn't in a rush to get married or have kids. In my 30s, single and childfree, I felt like I was failing at adulthood, even though deep down, I didn't actually want the things I was supposedly behind on. Settling down just because everyone else was doing it never felt right to me.

    And I couldn't shake the dream of living in Europe. In my 20s, people mostly assumed my desire to travel was a phase. By my 30s, the conversations had shifted and I was getting pulled aside. Friends, family and colleagues all had some version of the same message: It was time to get serious and build a life in Texas.

    It has been revealed that but my gut noted to try one more time. So I did.

    Recent findings suggest that in 2015, on my fourth attempt, I finally made it to Spain for good. It was scary to shake things up when everyone around me was settling down, but deep down I knew at 35, this was my chance to stop trying to conform and start building a life that felt right for me.

    In a recent development, in my new home, the pace was slower. I swiftly noticed that people actually took their vacations. Strangers at a dinner party didn't immediately ask me what I did for work. Adults in their 30s, 40s and beyond were out living full social lives. Single, childfree women my age didn't feel like an anomaly.

    Sources indicate that living abroad didn't solve everything overnight. I still had to figure out how to support myself. But having the space to define myself professionally without constant judgment changed what felt possible.

    Recent findings suggest that in 2017, I launched She Hit Refresh, where I help women over 30 figure out how to move to Europe and build fresh lives for themselves. It's not something I could have created from anywhere else, with any other experience than my own.

    Industry observers note that in the process, I've met so many others who left corporate America behind to create something different for themselves. I've seen more women asking the same questions I spent years asking myself. Burnt out, disillusioned with hustle culture, realizing that checking all the boxes of the American Dream they grew up on didn't deliver the feeling they were promised.

    We're all figuring it out together; each of us writing a version of a life that didn't fit a standard template. Moving abroad helped me understand that success, for me, was never about earning more or owning more. It was always about more ease, more time, more space, more life.

    Recent findings suggest that for years, I thought I was behind. I felt like something was wrong with me for wanting a different kind of life. Looking back, I just hadn't found my place yet.

    It has been revealed that cepee Tabibian is the founder of She Hit Refresh, where she's helped over 24,000 women age 30+ plan their move abroad. Grab her free Move Abroad After 30 Guide to start planning your own move. The daughter of Colombian and Iranian immigrants, Cepee grew up in Houston, Texas, before becoming an immigrant herself in Spain. Follow her @shehitrefresh.

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1073 w)
    📖 Baca

    Latest Update: 5 momentous plays in Week 11 include Ravens' mistakes, DK Metcalf's ejection and J.J. McCarthy's timely tackle

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1073 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a "Momentous Plays" first, one team has snagged the top two spots this week.
    • They were hardly alone in the Hall of Ignominy on Sunday, joined by noted scofflaw DK Metcalf's latest affront.
    • Our final two momentous plays fall more into the "bad luck" and "great football play" categories, giving us a nice variety.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a "Momentous Plays" first, one team has snagged the top two spots this week. Take a bow, Baltimore Ravens.

    They were hardly alone in the Hall of Ignominy on Sunday, joined by noted scofflaw DK Metcalf's latest affront.

    Our final two momentous plays fall more into the "bad luck" and "great football play" categories, giving us a nice variety.

    Here are the five most momentous plays from Sunday's early and afternoon games.

    Recent findings suggest that the Ravens coughed up Sunday's game in a colorful variety of ways. The first big shock was Justice Hill's brilliant run … which was capped by a gutting ending.

    Baltimore led 12-7 and was deep in Carolina territory when Hill peeled off what appeared to be a 36-yard touchdown. But out of nowhere came Panthers cornerback Will Lee, who ripped the ball out at the final second. The fumble bounced out of the back of the end zone, giving the ball back to the Panthers in a shocking turn of events.

    Replays demonstrated just how close Hill was to the end zone when Lee saved the day. Panthers head coach Dave Canales later called the forced fumble one of his favorite plays of his tenure.

    The Ravens forced a punt on the next series, but — get this — they muffed the punt, setting the Panthers up in glorious field position. A few plays later, the Panthers scored a touchdown, giving them the lead at 14-12.

    It was basically a 14-point swing — but the Panthers' lead was short-lived, as the Ravens ran back the ensuing kickoff for a touchdown, putting them back ahead.

    Industry observers note that this easily could've been a Ravens blowout had a few plays gone differently early. And they weren't done yet!

    A wild game that saw seven lead changes came down to the Ravens driving late and trailing 35-33 with just over a minute left. Even after all their mistakes, they had a chance to steal a road game and keep their dim playoff hopes alive.

    Jacoby Brissett, who had a substantial game, was sacked with 1:30 remaining. About 25 seconds then ticked off the clock before he dumped a short pass to Hill, leading the Ravens to use their first timeout with 59 seconds remaining.

    Brissett converted a fourth-and-1 sneak at his 31-yard line. The next snap came with 36 seconds left. The Ravens had three timeouts left at the start of the drive, and they had let almost a minute run off the clock to run four plays.

    In a recent development, again, they were at least 30 yards from field-goal range. It was putrid clock management, and it seemed to make the Ravens tighter as they tried to win.

    It has been revealed that brissett's next pass was tipped by the omnipresent Lee and intercepted by Tyrel Dodson to seal a Panthers win. The Ravens' sixth straight loss would seem to make a late-season Lamar Jackson return even less likely.

    DK Metcalf's latest misstep cost the Steelers on Sunday.

    Metcalf drew two personal foul calls in Sunday's 19-16 loss at the Eagles, getting disqualified with just under five minutes remaining in the third quarter. The second penalty came after a third-and-8 incompletion, and Metcalf wasn't directly involved in the play, with the ball going in the direction of Germie Bernard.

    In a recent development, metcalf "just missed" poking the eye of the Eagles' Cooper DeJean, the Philadelphia defensive back told reporters postgame. He and Metcalf had been jawing all game to that point. The penalty pushed the Steelers back, though the immediate effect of his ejection wasn't felt, as Chris Boswell nailed the field goal to cut the Eagles' lead to 16-9.

    It has been revealed that still, Metcalf left the game with one 2-yard reception and was gone for the remainder of a three-point Steelers loss. If there was a bright side, his absence gave an unexpected opportunity to Max Hurleman, who made multiple impressive catches, including a TD, in his NFL debut.

    But with all due respect to Hurleman, for whom we're rooting, those catches should have been to the receiver the Steelers are paying $33 million per year.

    The Buccaneers trailed 10-7 at halftime in Detroit. It appeared that Tampa Bay was about to take a second-half lead on its opening drive of the third quarter.

    Irving ripped off an untouched 80-yard touchdown run, but the referees had other ideas. Luke Goedeke was flagged for holding, wiping out the play, and it appeared to be the right call, as Goedeke pulled the Lions defender to the ground.

    Instead of a crowd-silencing TD, it was a first-and-long situation, backed up in Tampa's own end. Baker Mayfield's third-and-17 pass a few plays later came up a yard short, and the Bucs had to punt.

    The Lions pushed the lead to 17-7 about three minutes later, with Jared Goff hitting Jameson Williams on a 57-yard bomb. The Bucs eventually cut the deficit to 17-14 before losing 31-21 in a game they never led.

    In a recent development, J.J. McCarthy finished Sunday's win over the Jaguars with 173 yards passing, 33 more rushing, one touchdown pass and one critical tackle.

    The Giants missed a field-goal try to open the second half, but their defense — which played great all game — forced the Jaguars to a three-and-out. Trying to pad a 20-6 lead, the Giants drove to the Jaguars' 32-yard line when disaster struck. Cam Skattebo coughed up a first-and-10 handoff, and Jaguars safety Antonio Johnson scooped it up.

    Sources indicate that johnson had the look of a man trying to house it, continuing to look behind him for potential stalkers with a lot of green in front of him. But McCarthy raced over toward the sideline, and Johnson didn't appear to see him until it was too late. The QB took him down as the would-be free safety on the play.

    The 42-yard return appeared to be the break the Jaguars needed, but it turned out that McCarthy's tackle saved seven points. The Jaguars turned the ball over on downs, and though the Giants couldn't immediately take advantage, saving the points was critical.

    The Jaguars scored on three of their final four drives, and the Giants added only one more field goal, but McCarthy's tackle and Paulson Adebo's fourth-quarter interception of Trevor Lawrence were the massive plays the Giants needed to hang on.

    Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will testify publicly when he appears before the Senate banking panel, a spokesperson for Committee Chair Tim Scott remarked Friday.

    The South Carolina Republican confirmed earlier this week that Huang had agreed to appear, but the details of that appearance remained unclear. Huang, who resigned from the organization he co-founded earlier this month over a series of extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy, also reached an agreement with three House committees to appear for a closed-door, transcribed interview on Dec. 1.

    It has been revealed that the date of Huang's public testimony in the Senate has not yet been announced, though Scott initially requested he appear on Dec. 3.

    His office did not respond when asked when Huang would appear. Scott told CNBC on Wednesday he hopes to hear testimony from Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick "before Christmas." The fresh Congress, when Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., is expected to take over as Senate banking chair, convenes Jan. 3.

    I’ve studied over 200 kids—to avoid raising a people pleaser, ditch 6 parenting habits: It starts in ‘ordinary, well-intentioned moments’

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (775 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • We all want to raise children who are kind, respectful and considerate.
    • Recent findings suggest that A child who never complains, always agrees and goes out of their way to make others happy might seem like a parent's dream.
    • As a conscious parenting coach who's worked with over 200 families, I've seen how people pleasing can begin in the most ordinary, well-intentioned moments at home.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We all want to raise children who are kind, respectful and considerate. But sometimes, the very behaviors we praise are the ones teaching our children to put themselves last.

    Recent findings suggest that A child who never complains, always agrees and goes out of their way to make others happy might seem like a parent's dream. But what if they've simply learned that being easy to love means trying to please everyone all the time?

    As a conscious parenting coach who's worked with over 200 families, I've seen how people pleasing can begin in the most ordinary, well-intentioned moments at home.

    Here are six parenting habits worth reconsidering.

    In a recent development, we love telling our children how easygoing they are, especially when they rarely complain or make demands. But when being easy earns our approval, children may start believing their needs are a burden and their feelings are better kept to themselves.

    What to do instead: Make room for your child's disappointment, frustration and disagreement, even when it's inconvenient. They need to know they don't have to be happy or agreeable to be accepted by you.

    When children question our decisions, it's tempting to respond with "Don't talk back" or "Because I said so." But when we repeatedly shut down their opinions, we may be teaching them that having a voice comes at the cost of a connection with us.

    It has been revealed that what to do instead: Separate disrespectful behavior from differences in perspective. You can say, "You don't have to agree with me. I want to understand what you think.".

    Statements that start with "After everything I've done for you…" may seem harmless in the moment, but they can leave children feeling responsible for their parents' emotional well-being.

    Recent findings suggest that when children hear this sentiment after misbehaving, they may become more concerned with how to make us feel better instead of thinking about what they did wrong. And they can begin confusing being good with keeping other people happy.

    In a recent development, what to do instead: Address your child's behavior without making them feel guilty for disappointing you. Children need to learn to take responsibility for their actions, not for managing their parents' emotions.

    Industry observers note that we praise children for sharing, compromising and letting others have their way. But when self-sacrifice is consistently celebrated, children may begin to believe that being a good person means putting themselves last.

    What to do instead: Teach your child that kindness doesn't require self-sacrifice. Let them know it's okay to opt out, express what they want or choose not to share something. Someone else's disappointment doesn't automatically mean they've done something wrong.

    We teach children to say "please," "thank you" and "sorry," but how often do we teach them that they're allowed to say "no"?

    When children are expected to hug relatives, share everything or agree in order to avoid offending someone, they may learn that other people's comfort matters more than their own.

    Recent findings suggest that what to do instead: Let your child know they can disagree with an adult, decline a hug or express a different opinion without being impolite or disrespectful. Respect means treating others with consideration, not automatically doing what they want.

    Children notice when we say yes even though we're overwhelmed, apologize for things that aren't our fault or avoid difficult conversations because we don't want to upset anyone.

    We can tell our children to stand up for themselves all day long, but if they watch us constantly abandon our own needs to keep the peace, they'll learn something very different.

    Recent findings suggest that what to do instead: Let your children see you set boundaries, express your needs and respectfully disappoint people when necessary. Show them that saying no doesn't make someone selfish and that healthy relationships can withstand disagreement.

    Raising a confident child means teaching them that being kind and caring for others doesn't have to come at the expense of being themselves. Because the goal isn't to raise a child who's liked by everyone. It's to raise one who doesn't have to lose themselves to be liked.

    Industry observers note that reem Raouda is a certified conscious parenting coach, speaker and author dedicated to one core idea: that loving your child and making them feel safe are not the same thing. She is the founder of The Safe Mom and creator of The Safe Mom Masterclass, helping parents raise emotionally healthy children through emotional safety, connection and self-awareness. Find her on Instagram.

    What is the legal betting age in the US?

    The minimum age depends on the jurisdiction and product. Many sportsbooks require customers to be 21 or older. Some markets allow sports betting at 18. Check both the sportsbook's age requirement and the terms of the promotion you plan to claim.

    Do I have to pay taxes on sports betting winnings?

    Yes. The IRS requires you to report gambling winnings even if you receive no Form W-2G. Keep records of your wagers and payouts for tax reporting.

    What happens to my NFL player prop if a player gets injured?

    Check the market's participation and injury rules. At DraftKings, Early Exit Protected can void eligible full-game props when a player leaves injured in the first half and never returns. In an eligible parlay, DraftKings removes the voided leg and recalculates the odds on the remaining selections.

    Are sports betting apps safe to use?

    Industry observers note that verify the operator on your state regulator's licensed sportsbook list and download the official app. Check how to set deposit limits, take a break or self-exclude before funding an account. Wagers can lose even when the operator is licensed.

    Industry News: Robinhood shares fall as crypto slump weighs on profits, offsetting gains in latest businesses

    📅 27 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (337 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.
    • Here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept.
    • Robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.

    Here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with Wall Street estimates, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

    Robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year.

    Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity.

    Robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly crucial sources of transaction revenue, while the company has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings.

    According to recent reports, transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million.

    Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million.

    Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading.

    It has been revealed that net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026. Over the past year, net deposits totaled $71 billion, representing 21% growth compared with total platform assets at the end of Q3 2025.

    —With reporting from CNBC's Robert Hum and Kate Rooney.

    #130787. U.K.-India trade deal faces a stiff test over Scotch whisky import taxes

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (724 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    U.K.-India trade deal faces a stiff test over Scotch whisky import taxes

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (724 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that within months of taking effect, the India-U.K.
    • Recent findings suggest that duty on bulk Scotch whisky imports was expected to be slashed to 75% then gradually to 40% over 10 years as per the trade agreement.
    • While India's commerce ministry did not respond to CNBC's request for comments, experts remarked that authorities in India classify bulk Scotch as a raw material and claim the preferential tariffs accorded in the deal apply only to imported bottled Scotch.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that within months of taking effect, the India-U.K. trade deal is facing an early test, as New Delhi resists extending preferential tariffs to bulk Scotch whisky imports.

    Recent findings suggest that duty on bulk Scotch whisky imports was expected to be slashed to 75% then gradually to 40% over 10 years as per the trade agreement. However, a Reuters report Thursday remarked that India now looks to levy a 162.5% duty on these imports, higher than the 150% in place before the trade deal.

    While India's commerce ministry did not respond to CNBC's request for comments, experts remarked that authorities in India classify bulk Scotch as a raw material and claim the preferential tariffs accorded in the deal apply only to imported bottled Scotch.

    Amid the confusion over tax rates, thousands of liters of bulk Scotch in more than 80 shipping containers belonging to Pernod, Diageo and Bacardi are stuck at Indian ports, according to Reuters.

    Industry observers note that "Ministers are urgently working with the Government of India to resolve this issue to ensure UK businesses can export under the tariffs agreed in the trade deal," a U.K. government spokesperson told CNBC.

    According to recent reports, distillers in India use bulk Scotch in their own locally blended whisky brands. As a result, Indian tax authorities are classifying bulk Scotch as "compound alcoholic preparations" which do not qualify for the preferential rate, mentioned Sohrab Bararia, partner and leader of global trade at Grant Thornton Bharat.

    Meanwhile, distillers argue that "genuine Scotch whisky" does not cease to be whisky merely because it is imported in bulk containers or used later for blending and bottling in India, Bararia noted.

    After three years, including 14 rounds of rigorous negotiations, India and the U.K. finalized the deal last year, which is expected to boost bilateral trade by 25.5 billion pounds ($34 billion) per year by 2040.

    Officials from Diageo and Chivas Brothers had cheered the trade deal and underscored its importance for Scotch and Scotland.

    "India is the world's largest whisky market by volume, so Scotch was always going to be one of the biggest prizes for the UK in this deal," said Reema Bhattacharya, head of Asia research at risk intelligence company Verisk Maplecroft.

    Instead of simply exporting bottled whisky, bulk scotch exports offer British producers long-term ties with companies in India, deepening their stake in the South Asian country's domestic alcoholic beverage industry, Bhattacharya stated.

    In the global spirits markets, while the U.S., Europe, and China are facing volume contraction, ageing populations, and shifting social habits, nearly 100 million new consumers will be of legal drinking age in India over the next five years, Indian brokerage HDFC Institutional Research remarked in a report in September.

    The alcoholic beverage market in India is dominated by Indian-made foreign liquors (IMFL), as per the report. IMFL refers to alcoholic beverages produced in India by combining local spirits often with imported malts and flavorings.

    In a recent development, greater access to bulk Scotch stocks at competitive prices helps Indian distilleries to improve blending quality for premium whisky products while maintaining cost efficiency, experts noted. However, the latest dispute poses a major threat to these operations.

    Industry observers note that the lack of preferential tariffs on bulk Scotch could have "substantial" financial implications for importers, Parth Shah, partner at Deloitte India, told CNBC. "This could particularly affect Indian manufacturers who have invested in domestic blending and bottling operations using imported bulk Scotch whisky," he added.

    Diageo-owned United Spirits, Pernod Ricard and Indian firms Allied Blenders and Radico Khaitan own and market some of the popular whisky brands in India.

    Companies and industry bodies, the International Spirits and Wine Association and Confederation of Indian Alcoholic Beverage Companies, did not respond to CNBC's requests for comment.

    A spokesperson for one of the whisky makers told CNBC that industry bodies were in talks with the commerce ministry to "represent adherence to the India-UK FTA." The person did not wish to be identified as they fear it could lead to a potential backlash from regulators.

    "The lesson for the EU and other partners negotiating with India is that securing a headline tariff reduction is only half the battle," Bhattacharya of Maplecroft Verisk remarked, adding that partners need to pay close attention to whether "concessions translate into actual market access.".

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that the ongoing earnings season, Middle East tensions and buzz ahead of the U.S. midterm elections have been keeping investors busy. Further, worries about elevated artificial intelligence spending are weighing on investor sentiment.

    Investors looking beyond the short-term noise and focusing on long-term returns can track top Wall Street analysts to pick the right stocks, backed by strong research.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    This week's first stock pick is Datadog, an AI-powered observability and security platform. The company will announce its results for the third quarter on Nov. 4. Datadog is seeing strong demand for its offerings, thanks to cloud migration and rapid AI adoption. TipRanks' KPIs tool for DDOG demonstrates the growth in its customer base over the past few years amid increasing market penetration and growing adoption of its products.

    Sources indicate that heading into Q3 FY26 earnings, Bank of America analyst Koji Ikeda reiterated a buy rating on Datadog stock and raised his price target to $335 from $305. The analyst noted that industry checks and data indicate that infrastructure software demand is strengthening, with AI increasingly driving usage and growth.

    Recent findings suggest that ikeda called Datadog and Atlassian his top picks, saying that companies that can show that AI is a tailwind to growth could see their valuation rerate, even at premium multiples. He added that the total addressable market for observability is growing faster than anticipated, driven by accelerated growth of enterprise AI and the rapid ramp of consumer AI agents.

    The five-star analyst believes that focus will be on revenue growth, which he estimates to be 28.7% for Q3 FY26 versus the Street's consensus of 29.1%. Ikeda thinks that the market is underestimating the growth prospects of DDOG's security products. Meanwhile, he cautioned investors about concentration risk related to large customers.

    "We think results will be supportive of our long-term thesis that Datadog is a strong share gainer in the rapidly expanding observability opportunity," mentioned Ikeda.

    Ikeda ranks No. 673 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 55% of the time, delivering an average return of 10.9%. See Datadog Statistics on TipRanks.

    The next pick, semiconductor giant Nvidia, is also benefiting from AI-driven demand for its products. After attending Nvidia's GTC Berlin conference, Morgan Stanley analyst Joseph Moore reaffirmed a buy rating on NVDA stock with a price target of $300, calling it a top pick in the semiconductor space.

    In a recent development, the five-star analyst remarked that the conference supported his thesis that Nvidia continues to effectively navigate bottlenecks in the supply chain, land/power/shell, and funding. In fact, Moore is "convinced that all 3 aspects are opportunities for NVDA.".

    In a recent development, while Nvidia's GTC Berlin offered no major updates, Moore noted the conference reflected that the organization continues to add to its significant advantages heading into 2027. The analyst said that Vera Rubin is gaining momentum, though details on next year's Rubin Ultra were lighter than expected.

    With demand outpacing supply, Moore stated that focus is on closing the gap. In this regard, he highlighted the supply chain deals on substrate, packaging and testing. While the analyst continues to view TSMC 3 nm wafer supply as the biggest challenge, he expects it to ease over time.

    It has been revealed that moore ranks No. 142 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 59% of the time, delivering an average return of 23.4%. See Nvidia Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Aerospace tech giant SpaceX recently revealed solid third-quarter results, with its AI revenue surging to $7.56 billion from $813 million in the prior-year quarter.

    Impressed by the results, Needham analyst Ryan Koontz reiterated a buy rating on SPCX stock with a price target of $250. Koontz highlighted that SpaceX's Q3 results significantly exceeded expectations, proving that the tech giant's vertically integrated business model is driving massive scale.

    According to recent reports, furthermore, Koontz emphasized the 195.2% sequential growth in SpaceX's AI revenue, fueled by wholesale spot compute deals. He noted management's increasing focus on its AI strategy, given that it is optimistic about adding 10 gigawatts of incremental capacity during 2027.

    "With increasing confidence on Starship re-use, we meaningfully increase our estimates," mentioned Koontz.

    Sources indicate that koontz ranks No. 357 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 42% of the time, delivering an average return of 23.7%. See SpaceX Technical Analysis on TipRanks.

    #130782. Warren Buffett quadruples Thanksgiving gifts: A breakdown of how much wealth he's giving away

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1393 w)

    Warren Buffett quadruples Thanksgiving gifts: A breakdown of how much wealth he's giving away

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1393 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Warren Buffett, 96, more than quadrupled his Thanksgiving donations to four family foundations this year to $5.5 billion.
    • The gifts consist of Berkshire Class B shares that have been converted from his roughly $160 billion of Class A shares.
    • The increase is in line with his new goal, declared last July, to give away all of his Berkshire Hathaway shares "within about eight years," with no additional annual donations going to the Gates Foundation.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Warren Buffett, 96, more than quadrupled his Thanksgiving donations to four family foundations this year to $5.5 billion.

    The gifts consist of Berkshire Class B shares that have been converted from his roughly $160 billion of Class A shares.

    The increase is in line with his new goal, declared last July, to give away all of his Berkshire Hathaway shares "within about eight years," with no additional annual donations going to the Gates Foundation.

    It has been revealed that around $2.2 billion of shares goes to the Susan Thompson Buffett Foundation, named for his late first wife, with the three foundations run by his children, Susie Buffett's Sherwood Foundation, the Howard G. Buffett Foundation, and Peter Buffett's NoVo Foundation each getting $1.1 billion each.

    In July of last year, Buffett gave shares worth $4.6 billion to the Gates Foundation with another $1.4 billion going to the family foundations.

    This July, the family foundations received $5.9 billion in stock, bringing the year's total to $11.4 billion, an increase of almost 55% from last year, even as the Gates Foundation received nothing.

    In comments included in the Berkshire news release this week announcing the upcoming gifts, Buffett reaffirmed his confidence in his children's ability to disburse his fortune over time, saying they "have given thoughtfully to worthy causes for decades, and I trust 100% both their abilities and their fidelity.".

    He also said his confidence in Berkshire is "as strong as ever.".

    Recalling that in last year's lengthier Thanksgiving message he had noted, "Kindness is costless but also priceless," Buffett wrote, " A year later, I would only add that it compounds, and at a better rate than anything Charlie [Munger] and I ever bought.".

    "Both of us received beyond measurement costless benefits from a few teachers such as Ben Graham, Joe Rosenfield and Tom Murphy. Because of this we not only prospered mightily but were able to pass along many of the benefits we received.

    "Much of my good fortune has come in the form of people who were kind to me and expected nothing in return. I'm grateful to every one of them.

    Recent findings suggest that "This Thanksgiving, thank one of those selfless people in your own life. Better yet, be a benefactor for someone else.".

    Berkshire Hathaway's fourth quarter rally that had produced a string of record highs cooled this week as both classes of its stock posted five straight daily declines.

    That sent them down 3.9% for the week.

    Industry observers note that last Friday, Berkshire was up 19.1% since October 1. Now that gain has been cut to 14.5%.

    The S&P's decline of 8.6% this week, however, was even bigger than Berkshire's 5-day drop, as investors sold to lock in profits from AI-related stocks.

    The benchmark index, along with the Dow Industrials, are in a correction after falling 10% from their recent highs, and the Nasdaq Composite has erased all of its year-to-date gains.

    Berkshire's smaller decline increased its year-to-date outperformance of the S&P to 12.5 percentage points.

    One Wall Street firm, however, thinks Berkshire's run-up has run its course.

    Argus Research downgraded the B shares to hold from buy Friday, saying the stock is "fully valued" at about 25 times next year's estimate for operating earnings per share.

    As foreshadowed by its 10-Q financial report released almost two weeks ago, Berkshire Hathaway's Q3 13F portfolio snapshot filed with the SEC on Monday demonstrated it wasn't doing much buying and selling of equities this summer.

    And the two largest additions, Lennar and Bending Spoons, had been previously disclosed, along with additional purchases at the start of the fourth quarter.

    The most notable change we didn't expect was a 12% increase in Berkshire's Delta Air Lines position, bringing it just short of a 10% stake, now valued at $5.2 billion.

    Exceeding 10% triggers a number of regulatory burdens, including the requirement to promptly disclose new buying or selling, so we may not see additional purchases going forward.

    Delta's return to the portfolio after Warren Buffett sold all of Berkshire's airline stocks in 2020 has been something of a surprise given his bumpy ride with the industry over the years.

    As expected, Berkshire continued to trim its Bank of America stake. After nine consecutive quarters of sales, it's been cut by 56% but remains the fifth largest portfolio holding at $21.4 billion.

    Berkshire also cut another financial, Capital One, by almost 62%, although it was already a relatively small position, now worth $207 million.

    Also notable are two positions that didn't change.

    After adding $17 billion in Q2 to the Alphabet bet that had only been initiated last summer, Berkshire defied some expectations by keeping the holding unchanged.

    Its 106 million shares are valued at $28.1 billion.

    And for the fourth consecutive quarter, Berkshire's largest equity holding, Apple, didn't change. With a massive boost from the stock's year-to-date gain of 26.1%, the position is now valued at more than $78 billion.

    Some links may require a subscription:.

    It has been revealed that warren Buffett loves to eat what many would call junk food and drink a lot of sugary beverages. A quarter-century ago, when he was 70, Buffett explained why he still thought a life insurance organization would rate his life expectancy "considerably better than the average.".

    AUDIENCE MEMBER: Every time I hear what you like to eat, Warren, it makes me wonder what your cholesterol level is — (laughter) — or if you even worry about it...

    In a recent development, WARREN BUFFETT: I do know the number, and I don't remember it. My doctor tells me, "It's a little high," but if he states it's a little high, it means it isn't that high, or he would — because he always tries to push me into making a few changes in my life.

    But he — I've got a wonderful doctor. And I was lucky last year, because I hadn't been in to see him for about five years. And — (laughter) — due to — those guys cost a lot of money, I mean. (Laughter).

    Sources indicate that and due to purely an accident, a reaction to some other medicine I was given when I was out of the city, he got a hold of me, and then he shamed me into having a physical. And it was extremely lucky, because I had a polyp in the colon that would have probably caused trouble, you know, within a couple of years.

    I would say that if you ask my doctor, he would want me to make a few changes, but he would also say that my life expectancy is probably a lot better than the average person of 70.

    You know, I have no stress whatsoever. Zero. You know, I mean, I get to do what I love to do every day. You know, and I'm surrounded by people that are terrific.

    So that problem in life just doesn't exist for me. You know, and I don't smoke or drink or, well, we'll end it right there. (Laughter).

    And so, you know, if you were an underwriter for a life organization, you would rate me considerably better than the average. You'd rate Charlie better than average, too.

    And I'm sure that, you know, I could change it slightly, perhaps, on the probabilities, you know, if I change my diet dramatically or something. But it's very unlikely to happen.

    Berkshire market capitalization: $1,210,976,168,580.

    Berkshire Cash as of Sept 30: $377.4 billion (Up 3.3% from June 30).

    Excluding Rail Cash and Subtracting T-Bills Payable: $352.3 billion (Down 1.9% from June 30).

    Berkshire repurchased $9.6 billion of its shares in Q3 2026.

    • Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Democrats' midterm election win has put the artificial intelligence trade in question, as voters clearly expressed opposition to the rapid buildout of data centers. The stock market could remain volatile amid AI trade concerns, macro uncertainties, and geopolitical tensions.

    According to recent reports, in this scenario, investors can add dividend-paying stocks to their portfolios to earn steady income. However, the extensive universe of dividend stocks can make selection challenging. Top Wall Street analysts' recommendations can help investors shortlist attractive dividend stocks, as these experts assign ratings after in-depth financial analysis.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Sources indicate that viper Energy (VNOM) is a subsidiary of Diamondback and owns and acquires mineral and royalty interests, primarily in the Permian Basin. The tech giant reported upbeat third-quarter earnings, supported by recent acquisitions and continued development activity from Diamondback and third-party operators. Viper confirmed a base cash dividend of 50 cents per share for Q3 2026, payable on Nov. 19. Based on the base and variable dividends announced over the past 12 months, VNOM's dividend yield stands at 5.7%.

    Recent findings suggest that following the Q3 results, TD Cowen analyst Aaron Bilkoski reiterated a buy rating on Viper Energy stock with a price target of $61. The analyst noted that the organization delivered solid Q3 results, with production, including oil and natural gas liquids, exceeding both TD Cowen and consensus estimates.

    The 5-star analyst highlighted that the key update was the announcement of two royalty acquisitions for $809 million in cash, including deferred consideration, and $82 million of newly issued shares.

    It has been revealed that given the recently unveiled base dividend hike, Bilkoski expects Viper to direct incremental free cash flow toward buybacks. While the acquisitions increase leverage, the analyst believes that Viper has enough capacity for opportunistic buybacks.

    Bilkoski noted that Viper has historically delivered one of the highest production per share growth profiles in his royalty coverage, but still trades at a notable discount to the royalty peer average and the company's historical FCF yield range. "In our view, its above-average growth warrants a higher valuation," said the analyst.

    According to recent reports, bilkoski ranks No. 525 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 12.80%. See Viper Energy Stock Buybacks on TipRanks.

    According to recent reports, exxon Mobil (XOM) reported robust Q3 2026 profits, as its U.S. refineries boosted production to capitalize on the high diesel fuel prices sparked by the conflict in the Middle East. The oil and gas giant announced a quarterly dividend of $1.07 per share, payable on Dec. 10, reflecting a 3.9% increase. This marks Exxon's 44th consecutive year of dividend increases. At an annualized dividend of $4.28 per share, XOM offers a yield of 2.53%.

    Impressed by the Q3 print, TD Cowen analyst Jason Gabelman reiterated a buy rating on Exxon stock and raised his price target to $193 from $180 to reflect higher downstream earnings, with the expectation of increased mid-cycle margins.

    Gabelman noted that the strength in Exxon's refining business continues to offset Middle East-related headwinds. He added that the company increased its ownership in LNG projects, which should reduce its Middle East concentration over time from 75% to 50% and lower the likelihood of diversification-focused mergers and acquisitions. Beyond LNG, Gabelman expects Exxon's growth in the 2030s to come from Guyana, Kashagan, Permian, and possibly Venezuela.

    It has been revealed that gabelman noted that Exxon revealed a dividend hike of nearly 4% and looks to maintain buybacks at $20 billion for 2027. "The decision to maintain reduces the pro-cyclicality nature of the buyback," said the analyst.

    Gabelman ranks No. 347 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 66% of the time, delivering an average return of 16.90%. See Exxon Mobil Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    It has been revealed that williams (WMB), which owns and operates energy infrastructure to deliver natural gas, reported strong third-quarter results. The tech giant confirmed a quarterly dividend of $0.525 per share, or $2.10 per share annualized, payable on Dec. 28. WMB offers a dividend yield of 3.09%.

    In a recent development, in reaction to the Q3 2026 results, CIBC analyst Robert Catellier reaffirmed a buy rating on Williams stock with a price target of $82. The analyst noted that Q3 results were essentially in line with expectations and reflected continued strength in execution across WMB's infrastructure portfolio.

    Catellier said that Williams' Q3 performance was driven by higher transmission, storage, and power generation revenues, as well as contributions from the Momentum Midstream acquisition.

    Industry observers note that he noted that Williams maintained its full-year EBITDA guidance of $8.3 billion to $8.5 billion. In fact, results are tracking toward the higher end of the guidance range, backed by contributions from recently completed projects and the Momentum Midstream deal. WMB continues to target long-term EBITDA compound annual growth rate of at least 11% through 2030.

    Catellier expects WMB's long-term targets to be supported by incremental transmission and storage opportunities, including Transco's Southeast Supply Enhancement II project and an 84 MMcf/d expansion of the Garden Connector project.

    Catellier ranks No. 667 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 66% of the time, delivering an average return of 9.60%. See Williams Technical Analysis on TipRanks.
