    Berkshire breaks out to record high with fourth-quarter rally reaching 19%

    📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1107 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Berkshire Hathaway's red-hot shares are ending a strong week with four consecutive fresh record high closes.
    • Since the rally began with the start of the fourth quarter on October 1, the Class A shares have closed at record highs 11 times as they soared 19.1%.
    • The much more widely held B shares closed at upcoming highs just 10 times but are also up 19.1% from their near-term low.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Berkshire Hathaway's red-hot shares are ending a strong week with four consecutive fresh record high closes.

    Since the rally began with the start of the fourth quarter on October 1, the Class A shares have closed at record highs 11 times as they soared 19.1%.

    The much more widely held B shares closed at upcoming highs just 10 times but are also up 19.1% from their near-term low.

    The gains are in sharp contrast to the S&P 500's 1.2% dip as investors appear to be seeing Berkshire as a relatively safe haven amid worries about AI stocks and spending.

    Both Berkshire classes were up 3.9% on the week as the S&P advanced by 2.5%, its best week since early August.

    Berkshire's B shares are now 7.5 percentage points ahead of the benchmark for the year so far.

    After erasing their post-Buffett CEO announcement losses three weeks ago, Berkshire shares are now up almost 10% since last year's shareholders meeting.

    They've gained around 29% since last August's lows and are up around 18% year-to-date.

    Berkshire Hathaway is due to disclose its quarterly equity portfolio snapshot on Monday when it files its Q3 13F with the SEC.

    We won't know for sure until then, but numbers in the firm's third quarter 10-Q, released last Saturday, indicate Berkshire continued to reduce its Bank of America stake.

    It would be the ninth consecutive quarter of selling.

    As of June 30, Berkshire reported holding 483.4 million BAC shares valued now at $24.7 billion, it's fifth largest equity position.

    On June 30, 2024, before the selling began, Berkshire owned just over 1 billion shares valued at $41.1 billion.

    Since then, the number of shares in the portfolio has decreased by 53.2%, not including any Q3 sales, while the stock price has increased by 28.3%.

    If there had been no reductions, the position would be worth $52.7 billion.

    The belief Berkshire sold more BAC shares in the third quarter is based on a $372 million reduction in the cost basis for equities categorized by the firm as "banks, insurance, and finance.".

    The 10-Q also reports $2.2 billion of pretax gains from equity sales.

    Barron's notes Bank of America and American Express are the only financial stocks in the portfolio that have a cost basis low enough to generate a gain like that. Amex is one of the four stocks fresh CEO Greg Abel indicated would be held for "decades" to come in his February letter to shareholders.

    In any case, Berkshire's almost 23% stake in Amex would have required it to rapidly disclose any sales.

    Based on the numbers in the 10-Q, the warrants Berkshire received as part of a 2011 $5 billion investment in the bank that it used in 2017 to buy 700 million shares at $7.14 each, and BAC's average stock price in the quarter, Barron's estimates 30 to 40 million shares may have been sold.

    That would be roughly in line with the 30.2 million shares sold in the second quarter.

    Recent findings suggest that the case isn't as good, but Barron's thinks Berkshire may have bought more Alphabet shares in the period. That's based on a $2.3 billion increase in the cost basis for the category that includes Google's parent.

    Overall, it looks like it will be a relatively quiet quarter with $2.4 billion in equity purchases and $2.8 billion in sales.

    In the first quarter, Berkshire bought $15.9 billion and sold $24.1 billion of equities. In the second quarter, it purchased $23.5 billion and sold $3.7 billion.

    All those numbers exclude the organization's buybacks of its own stock.

    In a term sheet filed early Friday, Berkshire Hathaway notes it is selling more than 182 billion yen ($1.1 billion) worth of bonds with maturities between 2029 and 2056 and annual interest rates between 2.6% and 4.6%.

    Bloomberg points out the rates, compared to benchmarks, are higher than its previous sale this year.

    It quotes a fund manager as saying market sentiment "has become more sensitive," forcing issuers to make their offerings more attractive.

    In April, Berkshire sold 272 billion yen ($1.7 billion) of bonds.

    Berkshire uses the proceeds from the yen-denominated bonds to protect its ongoing investments in Japanese stocks from currency fluctuations.

    Some links may require a subscription:.

    Warren Buffett recommends Benjamin Graham's book, "The Intelligent Investor," and outlines what he considers Graham's three most key ideas.

    It has been revealed that WARREN BUFFETT: On investment books, if you're asking about that, I would recommend the first two books that Phil Fisher wrote back around 1960, "Common Sense [Stocks] and Uncommon Profits" and the second one ["Paths to Wealth Through Common Stocks"]. They're very good books.

    You know, I obviously recommend, first and foremost, [Benjamin Graham's] "The Intelligent Investor," with chapters eight and 20 are the ones that you really should read.

    It has been revealed that two of the — well, all of the important ideas in investing, really, are in that book, because there's only about three ideas. And those — two of them are emphasized in those two chapters...

    One is that — to think of yourself — to think of investing as owning a business and not buying something that wiggles around in price.

    And the second one is your attitude, which ties in with that, the attitude toward the market, that's covered in chapter eight. And if you have the proper attitude toward market movements, it's an enormous help in securities.

    And the final chapter is on the margin of safety, which means, don't try and drive a 9,800-pound truck over a bridge that states it's, you know, "Capacity: 10,000 pounds." But go down the road a little bit and find one that says, "Capacity: 15,000 pounds.".

    Berkshire market capitalization: $1,259,897,054,755.

    Excluding Rail Cash and Subtracting T-Bills Payable: $352.3 billion (Down 1.9% from June 30).

    Tech Report: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warns Americans of 'bumps in the road' after tech outages

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (340 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned Americans to prepare for "bumps in the road" after a set of damaging technology outages rocked air travel and systems like Microsoft Outlook.
    • Government officials have largely dismissed the prospects that the outages, which also slowed bank transactions, are linked to a coordinated or artificial intelligence cyberattack.
    • Clayton, however, said on CNN's "State of the Union" that outages may continue as companies and the government upgrade their systems to adapt to the AI age.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned Americans to prepare for "bumps in the road" after a set of damaging technology outages rocked air travel and systems like Microsoft Outlook.

    Government officials have largely dismissed the prospects that the outages, which also slowed bank transactions, are linked to a coordinated or artificial intelligence cyberattack.

    Clayton, however, said on CNN's "State of the Union" that outages may continue as companies and the government upgrade their systems to adapt to the AI age.

    "The American people should be prepared for a great deal of investment in upgrading our systems; they should be prepared for investment in cybersecurity, and they should be prepared that any time there is a step change in technology, a step change in both compute and applications, there will be bumps in the road," Clayton said.

    "You prepare by knowing that systems are going to be upgraded; they may be interrupted for a period of time and that companies and government are dealing with this on the front foot," he stated.

    Clayton's warning came as the U.S. prepares to celebrate Thanksgiving on Thursday, one of the busiest travel weeks of the year. A technology outage prompted a nationwide ground stop just over a week ago, which lasted for hours.

    The Federal Aviation Administration stated router upgrades caused a flood of data that led to the ground stop, and that there is no indication of a cyberattack.

    Separately, Microsoft stated the Outlook outage was caused by "an matter during an earlier network capacity upgrade.".

    Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent delivered a similar message on CBS' "Face the Nation.".

    Asked if Americans should be concerned about the security of their financial institutions, Bessent mentioned: "No, they shouldn't.".

    "The patches may cause a glitch," he said, referring to measures banks are taking to safeguard from AI. "I think the American people should think of it as a vaccine; your arm may hurt, you may feel a little bad the next day, but it increases your long-term immunity and resiliency.".

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that yemen's Houthis, backed by Iran, said Sunday that they had targeted Rabigh oil refinery in Saudi Arabia, in the latest sign of worsening hostilities in the region, as Iranian forces seek to pressure the U.S. into accepting its terms.

    The Houthis said they has directly hit the infrastructure, though the extent of the damage remains unclear, Reuters reported.

    The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said earlier in the day that it had "intercepted and destroyed" a drone launched by the Houthis toward Saudi Arabia's western region, which included some of the country's critical energy refining and export infrastructure.

    Rabigh, about 165 kilometers north of Jeddah on the kingdom's western Red Sea coast, hosts Petro Rabigh, a major oil refining and petrochemical complex, developed by Saudi Aramco and Japan's Sumitomo Chemical.

    Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Interior did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment.

    Sources indicate that gulf countries reported multiple attacks by Iran-linked forces over the weekend, even as the country's foreign minister remarked his government remains open to a negotiated end to the war. Bahrain authorities said an Iranian attack on a civilian industrial facility injured two people on Saturday.

    The string of attacks mark the latest sign of escalation in the regional hostilities since the war between the U.S.-Israel and Iran began in late February, as negotiators have so far failed to agree on terms to end the monthslong war.

    The conflict has drawn in countries in the Gulf region, disrupting energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz, which used to carry a fifth of the world's crude shipments prior to the war, pushing up global prices for oil and commodities.

    The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations reported another incident involving a tanker and military forces in the Gulf of Oman on Sunday, after two tankers were struck by unknown projectiles the day before. The maritime agency gave no further details about the incident, urging vessels to stay vigilant about the operational environment.

    Recent findings suggest that tehran has indicated its intention to end the war with the U.S. through diplomacy, but President Donald Trump has dismissed Iranian proposals. Both sides have been in indirect communication via Qatar.

    Recent findings suggest that in an interview to Fox News on Saturday, Trump warned that he was inclined to order military strikes against Tehran next year, if the two countries failed to finalize an agreement. The president blamed the Iranian officials for stalling while escalating hostilities after the U.S. elections.

    "They're more aggressive now than before the election," Trump said, describing Iranian officials as "professional tap dancers." "They talk all the time, all they do is talk," he added.

    Recent findings suggest that the president has previously remarked that Tehran wants a deal to end hostilities but not one that is "acceptable" to him. He has oscillated between favoring an agreement that would end the fighting and insisting that the U.S. does not need to rush into any deal and is not afraid of resuming more aggressive attacks.

    The Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi remarked Saturday after a two-hour meeting with visiting Qatari mediators that, "We are in contact with mediators, including the Qataris, both in person and virtually, and are holding the necessary discussions to see whether another opportunity can be given to diplomacy," according to Reuters.

    International benchmark Brent futures inched 0.22% lower to $92.35 per barrel in early Asia trading hours, while WTI crude was down 0.19% at $83.25 a barrel.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton stated the U.S.
    • Alice Huang, with whom ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang reportedly had a romantic relationship, was a key figure in Megaspeed International, a cloud computing firm that operates data centers across Southeast Asia linked to the fallout surrounding the leadership shake-up.
    • "There is an investigation ongoing into her firm and into her," Clayton told ABC on Sunday, adding that, "Nvidia chips, they are the jewel.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton stated the U.S. is investigating Alice Huang and her former organization, Megaspeed, as a report identified one of her associates as a key decision-maker at the Singapore-based company.

    Alice Huang, with whom ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang reportedly had a romantic relationship, was a key figure in Megaspeed International, a cloud computing firm that operates data centers across Southeast Asia linked to the fallout surrounding the leadership shake-up.

    "There is an investigation ongoing into her firm and into her," Clayton told ABC on Sunday, adding that, "Nvidia chips, they are the jewel. They are the absolute top that everybody wants, that's why we're focusing on this.".

    Alice Huang's associate, Chinese national Li Ming, who is now out on bail in Singapore, was "deeply involved" in Megaspeed's activities and took part in major decisions, The Wall Street Journal reported earlier on Saturday, citing people familiar with the matter.

    The Singapore charges against Li concern alleged false representations to Super Micro Computer, a U.S.-based firm with known links to chipmaker Nvidia, though Megaspeed is not named in those charges.

    According to recent reports, last week, the Commerce and Justice departments said that the investigation into Megaspeed began in 2024 over potential export-control violations. Their joint statement said Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security and Singapore law enforcement interviewed Huang during an on-site check in June 2025.

    The Justice Department later took the lead in the criminal investigation.

    Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CBS on Sunday that the administration was seeking answers from Nvidia about its chip sales to China, including who oversaw compliance and which levels of the company knew about the activity.

    According to recent reports, separately, The Newly introduced York Times reported Sunday that Alice Huang was in contact with an officer of a top Chinese intelligence agency from spring 2025 through fall 2026, citing people briefed on U.S. intelligence reports.

    Bloomberg reported last week that the Justice Department is investigating whether entities linked to Alice Huang helped smuggle Super Micro products to China.

    Li faces five charges in Singapore, including two counts of fraud by false representation, along with allegations involving the operation of a manufacturer he controlled, unauthorized bank-account access and another company director's duties.

    Prosecutors allege he falsely told Super Micro that the company would hold and lease the servers it purchased.

    The Journal reported that Li is out on bail and that his case is ongoing. He was offered bail of S$1 million in March 2025. The Singapore charges do not name Megaspeed.

    Earlier this month, Singapore's Ministry of Home Affairs said that police had found insufficient evidence to establish that Alice Huang committed offenses related to the possible inaccurate declarations under investigation.

    The ministry said she was issued a stern warning for providing information that police assessed as knowingly inaccurate and for downplaying her role at Megaspeed. It also said Singapore had not investigated her for espionage.

    Megaspeed has said it is a "legitimate and lawful business" and that Huang left the tech giant in August 2025.

    It has been revealed that the scrutiny is set to intensify in Washington. Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and the manufacturer's general counsel, Tim Teter, have agreed to closed-door, transcribed interviews with three House committees on Dec. 1 and Dec. 2, respectively.

    The committees said they want answers about Nvidia's role in allowing Chinese actors to access advanced chips and the involvement of a potential Chinese intelligence asset.

    Sources indicate that speaking to CNBC's Squawk Box on Sunday U.S. time, Ryan Fedasiuk, a former advisor for U.S.-China Bilateral Affairs at the State Department, noted that there was "still a lot we don't know" about the case.

    He noted lawmakers would likely focus on Nvidia's customer relationships and "who knew what at the firm when.".

    Fedasiuk added that there was "a very good chance" investigators would find that people at Nvidia knew their products could be used for restricted purposes. He characterized the existing evidence as containing "multiple" smoking guns.

    Nvidia has lost $2 trillion in value. Here's what options traders expect from earnings

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (517 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that jensen Huang's forced exit from Nvidia shocked Wall Street and Washington, wiped $2 trillion off its market value, and raised serious questions about national security and regulation of the AI complex.
    • With volatility in the stock near the highest since April 2025, options traders are now pricing a 7% reaction in the stock after its report, the biggest implied move going into an Nvidia report since February 2025, and well above the median move of 3.2% over the last eight quarters.
    • It has been revealed that implied volatility reached 68 Monday, compared to under 40 in early October, according to ThinkOrSwim data.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that jensen Huang's forced exit from Nvidia shocked Wall Street and Washington, wiped $2 trillion off its market value, and raised serious questions about national security and regulation of the AI complex. Traders, for the moment, must content themselves with the comparatively mundane business of Tuesday's earnings, and options traders are expecting massive moves.

    With volatility in the stock near the highest since April 2025, options traders are now pricing a 7% reaction in the stock after its report, the biggest implied move going into an Nvidia report since February 2025, and well above the median move of 3.2% over the last eight quarters.

    It has been revealed that implied volatility reached 68 Monday, compared to under 40 in early October, according to ThinkOrSwim data. Nvidia vol reached a multi-year high above 92 in the aftermath of President Trump's tariff Liberation day in April '25. In other words, the manufacturer that for much of the AI boom was the most reliable winner in the market, is now more volatile than all but 35 companies in the S&P 500.

    "Longer term, I see significant downside risk unless Nvidia can attract an exceptional leader, someone like Tim Cook or AMD's Lisa Su," Nigam Arora, founder of the Arora report, said in a text ahead of the organization's after-market report on Tuesday.

    In a recent development, since hitting all-time highs in October, Nvidia shares have fallen 35%, shedding $2 trillion in market capitalization along the way. Including Nvidia, there are only five companies in the S&P 500 worth more than $2 trillion. However, there is evidence that bulls have been holding out hope while bears snatch up profits: the ratio of open puts to call contracts has actually widened towards calls, according to Barchart data. The ratio is right now 0.87, down from a one-year high of 1.02 two weeks ago and the lowest since the first week of October.

    The most popular contract by volume on Monday was the 155-strike put expiring at the bell Monday, but the most popular trade for later expiry was the 160-strike call expiring Thursday, and the second-most-common purchase was the 190-strike call expiring Friday, SpotGamma data show.

    One catch is that most call contracts traded Monday looked like neutral to bearish positions opened by traders selling calls. Of the 5 million options traded on Monday, 3 million were calls, but more were likely opened by sellers than buyers. Of the $2.3 billion in options premium traded on Nvidia Monday, $1.2 billion was tied to puts, SpotGamma data show.

    With bears taking profits in puts the past month, there's another potential snag on open interest. There are very few open put contracts at or below the $157 level at which the stock closed Monday. That suggests any bad surprise would find many traders with little downside protection.

    By the same token, there's notable open interest in call contracts from the 175-strike and above, suggesting profit-taking on a bounce could limit Nvidia's recovery past levels it breached over the past week.

    Either way, Tuesday's earnings could provide fireworks.

    Jaguars stunned by Giants amid officiating controversy, questionable late-game decision from head coach Liam Coen

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1924 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Jacksonville Jaguars entered Sunday at 7-2 having emerged as a Super Bowl favorite out of the AFC.
    • The Latest York Giants doused them with a splash of cold water.
    • Plagued by red-zone woes, officiating controversy and a questionable late-game decision by Jacksonville head coach Liam Coen, the Jaguars fell 23-18 to the Giants.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Jacksonville Jaguars entered Sunday at 7-2 having emerged as a Super Bowl favorite out of the AFC.

    The Latest York Giants doused them with a splash of cold water.

    Plagued by red-zone woes, officiating controversy and a questionable late-game decision by Jacksonville head coach Liam Coen, the Jaguars fell 23-18 to the Giants.

    Jacksonville had a shot to tie the game with fourth-and-goal at the Fresh York 8-yard line and 3:40 remaining on the clock. New York led 23-15, and the Jaguars were down to one timeout.

    But instead of going for a potential game-tying touchdown and 2-point conversion, Coen opted to kick a field goal that cut the deficit to five points, apparently betting on the Jaguars' defense to get them the ball back.

    Trevor Lawrence and the Jaguars suffered a stunning loss to the Giants on Sunday.

    Recent findings suggest that they did not. Cam Skattebo ran for a first down before the two-minute warning with the Jaguars having exhausted their final timeout. The Giants were able to kneel out the remaining two minutes of game clock in victory formation.

    It added up to a jarring loss for the now 7-3 Jaguars on the heels of an aggressive trade deadline in which they made several major swings to bolster their hopes of a Super Bowl run. The Giants, meanwhile, improved to 6-3-1 to maintain their lead in the NFC East over the 5-6 Dallas Cowboys.

    It has been revealed that coen was asked about his decision to kick the late field goal in his postgame news conference. He cited analytics charts and described going for a touchdown as a "hope play.".

    "We talked about it a few times," Coen mentioned. "Our defense, they hadn't done anything up until that point. Everything about the charts and everything talked about it said kick the field goal, get within five points.

    "Go get a stop, and you feel pretty good about where you're at. Just executing that down-and-distance on a fourth down is kinda challenging. Especially, they're zero blitzing you every play, the ball's gonna come out. It's like a hope play.".

    Coen's comments Sunday stood in contrast to a previous discussion with Barstool Sports about a strikingly similar, but not identical hypothetical scenario.

    In that discussion, Coen was asked about whether to kick a field goal or go for it when down by eight points at the 8-yard line with one key caveat: "When you're up against the greatest quarterback of all time.".

    According to recent reports, "You've gotta go for it," Coen said. … "It's weird down there — and you're in an opportunity to score a touchdown, you're that close. We all know how hard it is to score in the red zone in this league. … I think you've gotta be aggressive there.".

    Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy is certainly not "the greatest quarterback of all time." It's not clear if Coen would have made a different decision if facing a different caliber of quarterback.

    The Giants were in control virtually from the start. They took a 10-3 advantage into the second quarter and a 20-6 lead into halftime. While McCarthy kept Fresh York's offense moving and scoring, the Jaguars repeatedly broke down in the red zone.

    Jacksonville's first three trips to the red zone produced 6 points courtesy of two field goals and a turnover on downs in the third quarter when a fourth-and-1 pass from Trevor Lawrence fell incomplete.

    Jacksonville's fourth red-zone trip produced controversy on a third-down effort to cut their deficit to one possession.

    They appeared to do just that when Parker Washington made a leaping catch in the back of the end zone and got both feet in bounds. But officials ruled that he didn't maintain control of the ball as he hit the ground.

    Coen used Jacksonville's last remaining challenge to challenge the call on the field. The ball moved in Washington's hands after Washington hit the ground, but he never appeared to lose control of it.

    According to recent reports, but officials didn't see enough to overturn the call on the field, and the ruling of an incomplete pass stood. The result was a fourth down in which the Jaguars settled for a field goal to cut their deficit to 20-9.

    Industry observers note that jacksonville finally cracked the end zone with a touchdown pass from Lawrence to Brian Thomas Jr. with 6:39 remaining. A failed 2-point conversion left the Jaguars facing a 23-15 hole.

    Then came the decision that will prompt plenty of questions for Coen.

    In a recent development, in the end, the Jaguars woke up on offense and limited the Giants on defense as they outgained Fresh York, 354 yards to 238. Lawrence completed 25 of 47 passes for 301 yards with 1 touchdown and 2 interceptions.

    Sources indicate that mcCarthy completed 18 of 38 passes for 173 yards with 1 touchdown. But he didn't turn the ball over as the Giants won the takeaway battle, 2 to 1.

    The result will leave the Jaguars with plenty to ponder ahead of a Week 12 home game against the Titans.

    The Giants do indeed have the ability to run the clock out.

    The discussion for this game will be Jacksonville focused. First it will be whether or not Parker Washington deserved a touchdown on his reception in the end zone that was ruled incomplete.

    The second will be Liam Coen's decision to be on the 8-yard line facing fourth down and opting to kick a meaningless field goal rather than trying to tie the game.

    Giants running back Cam Skattebo stated that he was retiring the backflip after what happened to Aidan Hutchinson tearing his ACL celebrating a sack.

    Skattebo picked up the first down at the two-minute warning. Jacksonville has no timeouts left, so this should be the ball game.

    The Giants running back celebrated the only way he knew how: with a backflip.

    The Giants are in the driver's seat needing a few first downs to seal with win against the Jaguars.

    On second and seven, JJ McCarthy hit rookie wideout Malachi Fields for the 19-yard gain. Jacksonville only has one timeout left.

    Sources indicate that the Jaguars were grooving down the field, but the offense stalled in the red zone. After several incompletions by Trevor Lawrence to the end zone, Jacksonville opted to kick the field goal.

    Cam Little connected on the 26-yard field goal. Jacksonville now trails 23-18 with 3:40 left.

    According to recent reports, after an incompletion on first down, JJ McCarthy hit Malik Nabers for an eight-yard gain. An offensive lineman was then whistled for unnecessary roughness for hitting a Jaguars defender late.

    After another incompletion, Upcoming York was forced to punt.

    Jacksonville gets the ball back down 8 with 5:47 left to go in regulation.

    It looked like it was going to be a broken play as Trevor Lawrence had time, but couldn't find anybody.

    According to recent reports, all of a sudden he fired it to the end zone and Brian Thomas Jr. had gotten wide open.

    Sources indicate that jacksonville decided to go for two. He floated it into the end zone but it was picked, which doesn't mean much for the stat sheet other than the attempt failed.

    Upcoming York leads 23-15 with 6:39 left to go.

    Giants rookie kicker Dominic Zvada had made a 53-yard field goal and missed a 32-yarder.

    Zvada lined up for a 43-yard attempt and drilled it.

    New York leads 23-9 with 10 minutes to go.

    Trevor Lawrence's tough day continues.

    He had an incompletion on first down, and then threw his second interception of the game.

    The officials in this game are certainly apparent.

    Newly introduced York picked up seven yards on first down, but it was called back due to offensive holding.

    It has been revealed that JJ McCarthy then had three consecutive incompletions. New York took 1:02 off the clock and punted back to Jacksonville.

    The Giants lead 20-9 with 11:15 left in the game.

    It looked like Parker Washington made his latest video game-esque catch, but it was ruled an incompletion.

    It has been revealed that replay on the broadcast had JJ Watt swearing that it was a touchdown. Even the rules analyst on the broadcast stated it should have been a touchdown. Jacksonville challenged the play and the ruling was upheld.

    While the Jaguars didn't get a touchdown out of it, Jacksonville did add three with a field goal.

    New York leads 20-9 with 12:17 left in the game.

    Newly introduced York's drive consisted of two incompletions and then JJ McCarthy scrambling for a massive 29-yard gain.

    It was erased by a holding call.

    On third and 16 McCarthy had his third incompletion of the drive and New York was forced to punt.

    Jacksonville takes over trailing 20-6 at the start of the fourth quarter.

    It has been revealed that jacksonville got down to the 11-yard line. Trailing 20-6 with a minute to go in the third quarter, Liam Coen opted to go for it.

    Trevor Lawrence stared down his target and tried to thread the needle to Jakobi Meyers, but the Giants defense was all over it for the turnover on downs.

    The Jaguars defense had been on the field for over five minutes. Jacksonville needing something and it came in the form of a Cam Skattebo fumble.

    Jacksonville scooped it, and the defender spun away from the line and took it back 42 yards to give the Jaguars great field position.

    Jacksonville couldn't capitalize on Newly introduced York's missed field goal. Trevor Lawrence had two incompletions sandwiching a one-yard gain by Bhayshul Tuten.

    Newly introduced York leads 20-6 with 9 minutes to go in the third quarter.

    Rookie kicker Dominic Zvada had made a 53-yard field goal already in the game. It looked like his 32-yard attempt was going to be easy, but he planted weird and ended up pushing it wide left.

    Giants head coach John Harbaugh is showing he trusts his rookie kicker.

    Dominic Zvada has been inconsistent this season, but nailed a 54-yarder toward the end of the first half to put the Giants up 20-6.

    Trevor Lawrence put on a magic show in the backfield. He eluded three different sets of pressure from the Giants and managed to get a pass off.

    Brenton Strange caught it even though it wasn't nearly enough for the first down, it was still impressive. It ended up being just a gain of four.

    After the two-minute warning, Jacksonville punted trailing 17-6.

    This might be Abdul Carter's breakout game. He has found a mismatch on the Jaguars' offensive line because he is consistently going after Trevor Lawrence in the backfield.

    Carter already has two sacks in the game and four tackles overall.

    Upcoming York drove the field against the Jacksonville defense.

    The Giants' nine-play, 66-yard touchdown drive ends with JJ McCarthy finding Malik Nabers in the back of the end zone as the wide receiver just manages to get his two touches in.

    Recent findings suggest that jacksonville's offensive drive stalled in the red zone. The drive was highlighted by a nice 21-yard grab by Parker Washington.

    According to recent reports, on third and 12, Trevor Lawrence fumbled the snap, but was able to recover it. He couldn't find anything downfield and took off. He only picked up 8 yards.

    Cam Little came on and nailed the 35-yard field goal to decrease the Giants' lead to four points.

    Latest York leads 10-6 early in the second quarter.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Shares of chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices close down 7.72% to $489.19 on Thursday after investment firm Hunterbrook Media issued a report alleging that the company "has its own China problem.".

    Hunterbrook disclosed that it had taken a short position in AMD.

    According to recent reports, the report claims that "after the U.S. blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT Systems, the company kept getting newer AMD firmware, which enables AMD chips to run in servers.".

    CNBC did not independently verify this information.

    Hunterbrook also said that newly introduced export rules in Washington could "tighten restrictions on AMD's foreign business," alleging that AMD "bills over 20% of its revenue to customers in China and Hong Kong," and "depends on a Chinese partner to finish most of its chips.".

    The allegations come amid investigations of rival chipmaker Nvidia over its sales to companies in Asia with ties to China. AMD has been viewed as a beneficiary of the uncertainty surrounding Nvidia.

    "The claims misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships," an AMD spokesperson noted in a statement. "AMD complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations. We remain focused on serving our customers and upholding the highest standards of integrity.".

    Sources indicate that lisa Su, CEO of AMD, told investors on the manufacturer's recent earnings call that China is an "important" market and that the semiconductor giant wants to be fully compliant with U.S. export controls.

    AMD continued to slide after hours, trading down 0.45% to $487 shortly after 4 p.m.

    • Investors had been looking forward to the Anthropic IPO as a "clearing event" — reviving the tech sector after months of choppy trading, the Nvidia espionage scandal, and growing concerns that AI chip sales to Asia are likely to slump as Washington cracks down on potential violations of export controls.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that anthropic's historic IPO — the largest in U.S. history — delivered a significant win for the organization and its investors. But it failed at another task: reviving animal spirits in the AI trade.

    The Nasdaq Composite closed down 2.25% amid a broader market pullback with the S&P 500 declining 2% to 7,175.

    It wasn't supposed to play out this way.

    Investors had been looking forward to the Anthropic IPO as a "clearing event" — reviving the tech sector after months of choppy trading, the Nvidia espionage scandal, and growing concerns that AI chip sales to Asia are likely to slump as Washington cracks down on potential violations of export controls.

    Sources indicate that some of those worries resurfaced Thursday as a short seller, Hunterbrook Media, alleged in a report that firmware sold by chipmaker AMD had turned up in U.S.-blacklisted companies. AMD stock closed down more than 7%. The chipmaker told CNBC it complies with U.S. law.

    Adding to the worries, the House Foreign Affairs Committee released documents showing that a subagency of the Commerce Department approved the sale of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies. That also raised the prospect of an Asia sales slowdown under stricter export controls.

    Many investors and analysts continue to express confidence in the AI trade, noting that Anthropic's successful market debut — the stock closed up 17% from its IPO price and raised more than $81 billion — bodes well for capital spending across tech.

    But investors acknowledged that this is a high-tension moment and mentioned it's time to be more strategic about the trade.

    Dan Niles, founder of Niles Investment Management, described himself as a "circumspect bull," making the comparison to market conditions in 2022 when the big indices tanked in the back half of the year.

    Recent findings suggest that "You could have still made money that year. You just needed to have the right combination of longs and shorts," he said.

    It has been revealed that part of the challenge, Niles said, has been a price war between the two cutting-edge frontier labs, Anthropic and OpenAI. That has posed a threat to the overall revenue and profit potential of AI and the capex going into it. Fierce competition on price is producing collective losses between the two top companies, he notes.

    Sources indicate that "The combined revenue growth for OpenAI plus Anthropic went from growing 75% sequentially in Q2 to 48% in Q3," he told CNBC. "The combined losses went from $7.9 billion to about $8.4 billion from Q2 to Q3.".

    While uncertainty is high now, some resolution may be on the horizon if a greater degree of commercial and regulatory clarity emerges over the next few months.

    Trading experts also told CNBC that the tech sector's troubles Thursday were a more serious matter than Anthropic simply siphoning capital from other parts of the market.

    "There's a reset of AI in general," said JJ Kinahan, senior vice president at Cboe Global Markets.

    Investors for years have profited in tech by buying the dip, he said, but "there's been an attitude change that [you] can't buy things blindly and they'll all go up." Nvidia's ongoing declines have shaken confidence in the buy-the-dip strategy, he said.

    Industry observers note that anthropic's next few trading days will be a key gauge of the market's strength. Friday will be a "wild card," Kinahan remarked. It could be a "final flush out" for the market, or a bounce that leaves the market in "no man's land" while volatility remains elevated.

    A better gauge may be Monday, when options on Anthropic start trading, providing insight into whether retail investors will back the firm in force — providing more of a vote of confidence in the AI trade.

    "If people think we're going up [on Anthropic] they'll buy stock, but retail particularly will just buy calls," he remarked. "There's a bigger test coming Monday.".

    For now, investors continue to sell AI-related stocks.

    Neoclouds, the generally highly indebted AI-dedicated computing providers at the outer edges of the AI trade, were down substantially Thursday, with CoreWeave closing down more than 6%.

    Hyperscalers such as Alphabet and Amazon.com, viewed as relatively defensive AI bets, also finished lower.

    In a recent development, one bright spot: Cybersecurity stocks continued to rally, with Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike both closing up. AI is finding security holes across software infrastructure, creating a scramble to patch the vulnerabilities before hackers can exploit them.

    — CNBC's Daren Fonda contributed reporting.

    Cathie Wood’s Ark Invest was a major buyer of Anthropic as she tells CNBC she’s ‘quite optimistic’

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (422 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Cathie Wood was a major buyer of Anthropic following its debut Thursday on the Nasdaq, adding shares in all her major funds.
    • Wood's firm, which already owned private shares of the artificial intelligence company in its Ark Venture Fund leading up to the initial public offering, bought $90.8 million worth of Anthropic in six funds, according to a trade notification from the firm.
    • Recent findings suggest that "We've owned Anthropic since early '23," Wood told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Friday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Cathie Wood was a major buyer of Anthropic following its debut Thursday on the Nasdaq, adding shares in all her major funds.

    Wood's firm, which already owned private shares of the artificial intelligence company in its Ark Venture Fund leading up to the initial public offering, bought $90.8 million worth of Anthropic in six funds, according to a trade notification from the firm.

    Recent findings suggest that "We've owned Anthropic since early '23," Wood told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Friday. "It's our best performing equity by far in ARKVX, our venture fund. ... Our confidence has grown with time as it really took over the enterprise" AI business.

    It has been revealed that anthropic shares jumped 17% in their first day, but closed well off the highs of the session and were headed for sizable losses Friday. The Nasdaq, which was expected to get a boost from a major IPO reviving enthusiasm about the technology trade, fell by 2% on Thursday.

    Industry observers note that "We're climbing a wall of worry," said Wood. "Everybody is worried about AI hype and the political situation after the election, but I think we'll look back and say, OK this is more like the '80s and '90s, climbing a wall of worry you know with bricks much like what we have today: inflation, interest rates, wars, fresh technologies and so forth so quite optimistic here.".

    The Anthropic stakes are relatively small across the funds, but Wood typically will buy shares in companies she likes steadily during long stretches. Wood stated she is "averaging down" with her purchases of Anthropic.

    It has been revealed that in her $6.1 billion Ark Innovation ETF, Anthropic is a 0.3% stake. The biggest holdings in that fund are Tesla and SpaceX, representing more than 21% of the fund together.

    Ark Innovation, which retail investors piled into during the pandemic as it gained about 150% in 2020, tumbled the subsequent next two years, losing 67% in 2022 alone. Wood's following was dented after the significant losses.

    Recent findings suggest that the fund had a comeback stretch as the bull market revved back up from 2023 to 2025, but has fallen on hard times again this year, down more than 10% in 2026. The S&P 500 is up 4.8% this year.

    Wood dismissed comparisons of today's environment to the dot-com bubble.

    Sources indicate that "Back then if an Anthropic had gone public, it probably would have gone up threefold the first day," she stated. "That's how crazy things were.".

    #130668. As Anthropic shares tank, investors scramble to hedge. It could be very expensive

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (435 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    As Anthropic shares tank, investors scramble to hedge. It could be very expensive

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (435 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that as Anthropic shares tumble toward their IPO price of $83, investors are looking for ways to hedge.
    • If Anthropic breaks its IPO price, it will represent a 27% decline from Thursday's intraday high of $113.
    • Options traders are also looking at how SpaceX traded in the days following its offering for clues on how options might price.

    Recent findings suggest that as Anthropic shares tumble toward their IPO price of $83, investors are looking for ways to hedge. Unfortunately, they may have to wait until Monday, when options on the AI giant are expected to list.

    If Anthropic breaks its IPO price, it will represent a 27% decline from Thursday's intraday high of $113. The wild price swings offer clues on how expensive it might be to buy protection on the new tech giant once options begin trading.A 20% intraday move points to an implied volatility somewhere between 100 and 150 for Anthropic options, according to estimates from single-stock market-makers on the Cboe trading floor in Chicago.

    Options traders are also looking at how SpaceX traded in the days following its offering for clues on how options might price.

    Sources indicate that implied volatility in SpaceX started at 116, but that didn't deter options traders significant and small from piling into the contracts tracking the stock, with about 1.7 million contracts traded on the first day for a total options premium of about $2.5 billion. Far out-of-the-money call contracts were some of the most popular trades as the stock soared 40% in its first three sessions.One key difference between now and then? Anthropic is trading against the backdrop of S&P 500 volatility close to 30, compared to 17.3 when SpaceX debuted. "I expect ANT options to be super active," remarked Tom Sosnoff, co-founder of the trading platforms ThinkOrSwim and TastyTrade. "I expect heavy options volume."One thing Anthropic and SpaceX have in common is heavy retail involvement in both IPOs, with retail brokerages receiving a 20% allocation from SpaceX and reports pointing to between a 15-20% allocation from Anthropic on Thursday. "Round one of the Anthropic IPO easily goes to the individual investor," Sosnoff added. "Retail participants bailed early at the best prices of the day while institutional investors paid up to top off their underwhelming allocations. I believe retail was aggressively reloading in the mid-90s."Further signs of retail demand will become evident when options likely begin trading on Monday. One thing to watch: the spread between out-of-the-money call and put contracts, which was heavily skewed toward calls in the case of SpaceX. "I would be careful comparing Anthropic to SpaceX," said Dennis Davitt, CIO and Co-Founder of Millbank Dartmoor Portsmouth. "From a market-structure perspective, the two are dramatically different. The availability and cost of borrowing will be different, the companies are at very different stages of maturity, and SpaceX has allowed employees to monetize portions of their holdings over time. All of those factors matter when pricing options.".

    Prediction markets outlook for stocks in 2026 dims amid AI sell-off

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As stocks continue their tech-driven sell-off, prediction markets traders are seeing a bleaker outlook for the remainder of the year.
    • Industry observers note that on platform Kalshi, speculators place just 6% odds that the S&P 500 will cross 8,000 in 2026.
    • Contracts ask traders if the S&P 500 will go above various levels in 2026, and they're resolved using data from S&P Dow Jones Indices.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As stocks continue their tech-driven sell-off, prediction markets traders are seeing a bleaker outlook for the remainder of the year.

    Industry observers note that on platform Kalshi, speculators place just 6% odds that the S&P 500 will cross 8,000 in 2026. On Oct. 13, those odds were as high as 72%.

    Contracts ask traders if the S&P 500 will go above various levels in 2026, and they're resolved using data from S&P Dow Jones Indices.

    Sources indicate that on Friday, the Nasdaq Composite turned negative for the year as investors continued to dump tech stocks, primarily those with exposure to the artificial intelligence build-out. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500 fell into correction territory, too.

    The S&P 500 has slashed its year-to-date gain to just over 2%.

    The Stock Trader's Almanac in a Thursday note broadly agreed that the hopes for a December rally are fading, with the caveat that a "Santa rally" could still appear at the end of the year.

    📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1564 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    Vikings' defense has first poor outing of season as 49ers dominate in easy win

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1564 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, kirk Cousins of the Minnesota Vikings is hit by Nick Bosa of the San Francisco 49ers.
    • The Minnesota Vikings had high hopes after last week, when Kirk Cousins joined the team and they blew out the Green Bay Packers.
    • Recent findings suggest that sunday night was a good time to measure where the Vikings stood in the NFC hierarchy.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, kirk Cousins of the Minnesota Vikings is hit by Nick Bosa of the San Francisco 49ers. (Photo by Manuel Velasquez/Getty Images).

    The Minnesota Vikings had high hopes after last week, when Kirk Cousins joined the team and they blew out the Green Bay Packers. With the Vikings' defense playing very well yet again and Cousins providing much better play at quarterback in his first game with Minnesota after coming over in a trade, entering the Super Bowl discussion seemed reasonable.

    Recent findings suggest that sunday night was a good time to measure where the Vikings stood in the NFC hierarchy. And they found out there's a big gap between them and the San Francisco 49ers.

    In a recent development, the 49ers have looked like a Super Bowl contender since Week 1 when they blew out the Los Angeles Rams in Australia, and that domination continued in Mexico City on Sunday night. The 49ers handled the Vikings with surprising ease. They improved to 9-1 with a 35-10 win.

    The Vikings (7-3) are still in good shape. But their defense finally revealed some vulnerability and their offense took a step back from the first game with Cousins. Minnesota could still win the NFC North and make a deep playoff run, but Sunday showed there's a long way to go to reach the 49ers' level.

    The Vikings' defense was in trouble from the first drive. The 49ers moved the ball without any problem downfield and then tight end George Kittle scored on a 17-yard touchdown. The ease in which the 49ers moved the ball was surprising because nobody had been able to move it like that on the Vikings. The Vikings were so dominant, they held the Bears and their explosive offense to three points in Week 2. But the Vikings had no answers for the 49ers.

    Coordinator Brian Flores brings extra pass rushers way more than any other defense in the NFL, and once the 49ers figured out how to combat that by Brock Purdy getting the ball out swiftly, Minnesota's defense wasn't so scary anymore.

    Sources indicate that the 49ers scored touchdowns on three of their first four drives. Minnesota hadn't allowed more than 23 points in a game all season and the 49ers had 21 before halftime when Mike Evans made a great catch in the end zone, though there was a question if he had control with both feet down. It didn't matter because the touchdown call stood and at that point the Vikings were in danger of the game slipping away.

    Then Cousins made a mistake before halftime that practically finished the game before halftime.

    It has been revealed that the Vikings trailed 21-10 when 49ers safety Ji'Ayir Brown read Cousins and the Vikings' play perfectly and jumped in front of a pass intended for Tai Felton. Brown picked it off and had an easy 18-yard return for the touchdown.

    Minnesota's defense having its troubles with Purdy and the 49ers was the key to the game but the Vikings' offense struggled too. They got a touchdown in the first quarter and didn't get another the rest of the game.

    The Vikings are known for pressuring quarterbacks, but it was the 49ers who had constant pressure on Cousins. NBC's cameras found Cousins in an animated discussion with tackle Brian O'Neill on the sideline, seemingly telling O'Neill he was being hit every play. Without much of a running game or protection on pass plays, it was tough for Cousins to function.

    It has been revealed that the Vikings are still one of the NFL's better teams. They just had a tough matchup against a 49ers team that has a great argument as the best in the NFL. There's a long way to go in the season. That gives Minnesota time to figure out how it can match up better with San Francisco the next time, if they happen to meet in the playoffs.

    And we're officially done in Mexico City. The 49ers are now a near-perfect 9-1 after the win, which marked their third straight.

    The Vikings hold a 7-3 record, and have lost three of their last four. They are 1-1 now with Kirk Cousins as a starter after the deadline trade.

    Carson Wentz is in for the Vikings now, and Brock Purdy's day is done, too, as we hit the two mintue warning.

    The 49ers couldn't extend their drive to kill the game here, and got stopped on third after Deebo Samuel was stopped a few yards short of the first.

    Minnesota will take back over with 3:46 to go, but this one is over.

    The Vikings got all the way to the SF 20, but their attempt on fourth down was stopped just a few yards short of the line to gain.

    They needed a touchdown there to stay alive. Instead, Kirk Cousins is headed back to the sidelines down by 25 with just 8:16 to go.

    Sources indicate that and that should do it. Christian McCaffery punched in a 6-yard score one play after making his first catch of the night, and the 49ers are now up 35-10.

    That was a 98 yard drive for San Francisco.

    It was a scoreless third period, but San Francisco is knocking on the red zone looking to extend its lead.

    If they can add seven more here, this game will essentially be over. The Vikings absolutely need a stop.

    According to recent reports, the 49ers were all over Tai Felton there to break up the pass, and the Vikings will now have to punt. That was a long 10-play drive, but htey only made it 36 yards before having to punt.

    Minnesota will have to get points on the board here soon if it's going to mount a comeback.

    Sources indicate that the Vikings defense has responded yet again. They forced a quck three-and-out, and put too much pressure on Brock Purdy in the backfield there on third down for him to get a good throw off.

    Minnesota will get another shot with the ball here in the second half.

    Industry observers note that justin Jefferson looked like he had a path to the end zone there, but he did not have a firm grip on the ball at all. Deommodore Lenoir easily punched the ball out of his hands to force the early turnover.

    According to recent reports, san Francisco has suddenly taken back over. That's not the start Minnesota needed.

    Sources indicate that the Vikings have received the kick, and the second half is underway. We'll see if they can rally here.

    Industry observers note that the 49ers weren't able to score there, but they've been dominating so far tonight in Mexico City. Brock Purdy has thrown for 176 yards and three touchdowns already, two of which went to George Kittle.

    Minnesota will get the ball to start the second half. The Vikings attempted a 71-yard field goal just before half, but it was just barely short. That was only the 10th 70+ yard attempt in NFL history.

    Industry observers note that san Francisco will have a chance to put up more points before half. The 49ers forced a quick three-and-out there, so the Vikings will have to put with 68 seconds left before the break.

    One more touchdown before half would blow this game wide open.

    Industry observers note that what a turn for the 49ers! On the first play after Mike Evans' touchdown, Ji'Ayir Brown jumped up and intercepted Kirk Cousins to set up an easy trot into the end zone.

    All of the sudden, their lead is 28-10.

    Recent findings suggest that what a grab from Mike Evans! Brock Purdy found him in the back corner, and he hauled that ball in with just one hand perfectly.

    The 49ers lead 21-10 now with 2:09 left in the half.

    It has been revealed that colton McKivitz went down with what appears to be a significant ankle injury. His ankle was going off the wrong direction, and teammate Trent Williams slammed his helmet there after seeing it up close.

    He's being carted off now, and the entire 49ers team came over to see him off.

    In a recent development, the Vikings had to settle for a 48-yard field goal there after their drive stalled out. They converted on fourth-and-short earlier to keep it alive, too.

    Recent findings suggest that but points are points. The 49ers lead 14-10 now with 6:48 left in the half.

    George Kittle had to power through Harrison Smith to make the grab, but he's now got his second touchdown of the night. What a catch.

    The 49ers lead 14-7 now early in the second.

    We're all tied up after the first quarter in Mexico City, but the 49ers are driving once again. Brock Purdy just found Mike Evans for a 34-yard gain right up the middle, and they're in the red zone.

    According to recent reports, just like that, the Vikings have tied this game up. Aaron Jones capped the nine-play drive with an 11-yard touchdown run up the left side.

    Sources indicate that nick Bosa nearly got his first sack of the season on Kirk Cousins on the play right before the score, too. But instead, he was hit with a penalty for drilling Cousins in the backfield.

    It's 7-7 now with 1:13 left in the first.

    According to recent reports, investors often favor dividend stocks for their regular income and the promise of potential share price appreciation. But selecting the right dividend stocks from a huge pool of companies can be difficult.

    Top Wall Street analysts can help shortlist attractive dividend-paying stocks, as their recommendations are backed by thorough analysis of a manufacturer's financials.

    According to recent reports, devon Energy (DVN), an independent oil and natural gas exploration and production company, reported better-than-expected third-quarter results. The company confirmed a quarterly dividend of 32 cents per share for the fourth quarter, payable December 30. Based on the fixed dividends paid over the trailing 12 months, DVN yields 2.85%.

    After hosting a virtual investor meeting with management, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on Devon, with a price target of $59. Mehta stated that he is now more confident in management's outlook for delivering strong near-term capital returns as well as efforts to drive operational efficiencies and productivity gains.

    Devon sees an opportunity to increase share repurchases, driven by solid free cash flow (FCF), contributions from the Eagle Ford divestiture and continued improvement in the balance sheet, Mehta said. Devon expects share buybacks worth more than $1 billion in Q4 2026, up from $414 million in the third quarter, backed by a strong pricing backdrop and improved capital efficiency.

    Recent findings suggest that mehta, a 5-star analyst, mentioned Devon expects about $6.3 billion of excess FCF in 2027, including about $3.5 billion of net proceeds from the Eagle Ford sale. That would enable the manufacturer to accelerate buybacks while progressing toward its goal of reducing gross debt to about $9 billion by early 2027. Mehta noted that under DVN's framework to return up to 70% of annual FCF, management favors share buybacks as it believes the stock is discounted compared to large-cap peers.

    "Management expects continued capital efficiency gains from merger synergies, extended laterals, surfactant adoption and development of the newly acquired federal acreage," Mehta said.

    Mehta ranks No. 876 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 8.1%. See Devon Energy Stock Buybacks on TipRanks.

    Energy Transfer (ET), is a limited partnership that operates about 140,000 miles of pipeline and associated energy infrastructure. The company recently confirmed third-quarter results showing net income per common unit growing about 18% year-over-year, to 33 cents. ET's cash distribution for Q3 2026 was 34.25 cents per common unit, up more than 3% year-over-year. At an annualized distribution of $1.37 per share, Energy Transfer yields more than 7%.

    TD Cowen analyst Jason Gabelman reiterated a buy rating on Energy Transfer with a price target of $25. The company delivered better-than-expected Q3 results and declared the 1.2 billion cubic feet per day (bcf/d) South Mississippi Pipeline, a 215-mile, 36-inch natural gas line linking the Perryville Hub to the Florida Gas Transmission (FGT) network, Gabelman remarked. The project is supported by 20-year firm transportation agreements and is expected to enter service in 2030. ET expects to ultimately own 51% of the $1.6 billion project.

    Industry observers note that the 5-star analyst said that Energy Transfer lowered its 2026 capital spending outlook to $5.5 billion (midpoint of the guidance range) from $5.75 billion due to project timing. Energy Transfer expects capex to rise to $7 billion in 2027, while Gabelman projects $5 billion in both 2028 and 2029, based on disclosed projects.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • San Francisco 49ers right tackle Colton McKivitz left Sunday's dominant win over the Minnesota Vikings due to what looked like a significant injury to his lower left leg.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    San Francisco 49ers right tackle Colton McKivitz left Sunday's dominant win over the Minnesota Vikings due to what looked like a significant injury to his lower left leg.

    According to recent reports, the injury took place during the second quarter of the 35-10 win that was held in Mexico City. McKivitz's left leg got pinned under multiple players at the end of a Christian McCaffrey run.

    When McKivitz pulled his leg from underneath the pile of players, his foot was twisted in the wrong direction.

    Warning: Video below indicates a graphic injury.

    McKivitz's teammates immediately knew he had sustained a significant injury. Multiple players took a knee around their injured teammate, and left tackle Trent Williams slammed his helmet into the turf, then held the back of his head in his hands.

    Trainers rushed onto the field to tend to McKivitz. He was eventually taken off the field on a cart. He was upright and interacting with his teammates as they saw him off the field.

    The nature of McKivitz's injury wasn't initially clear.

    McKivitz is key to San Francisco's top-ranked offense. He's a strong run blocker who hasn't allowed a sack this season.

    Recent findings suggest that the 49ers have thrived despite injuries to key players on both sides of the ball this season, and Sunday night was no exception. They entered halftime with a 28-10 lead and cruised the rest of the way to secure the 25-point win. Brock Purdy went 21-of-26 for 255 yards with three touchdowns, two of which went to George Kittle.

    They now sit at 9-1 on the season after the win, which marked their third straight.
